<P class="p558 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p576 ft5"><SPAN class="ft31">“Third Party Agreement” </SPAN>means an agreement pursuant to which Third Party Financing is contributed to a Fund under the Platform, as defined in Article 2 of Annex I <SPAN class="ft47">“Receipt of Third Party Financing” </SPAN>to these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p566 ft5"><SPAN class="ft31">“Third Party Financing” </SPAN>means funds contributed to a Fund under the Platform by a Third Party, subject to the provisions of Annex I <SPAN class="ft47">“Receipt of Third Party Financing” </SPAN>to these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p577 ft5"><SPAN class="ft31">“Unitary Fund” </SPAN>means the pooled investment portfolio established by the EIB by the Deed Poll of 1 July 2009, as supplemented and amended from time to time and as defined in the corresponding Information Memorandum.</P>
<P class="p138 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">1.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Interpretation</SPAN></P>
<P class="p422 ft5">Subject to Article 1.1 of these Platform Rules and save where the context otherwise requires:</P>
<P class="p578 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">capitalised terms and expressions defined in the Preamble have the same meaning throughout these Platform Rules, unless herein otherwise defined;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">words denoting:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p579 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">the singular number only shall include the plural number also and vice versa;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p518 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">one gender only shall include the other gender; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p518 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">persons only shall include firms and corporations and vice versa.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p578 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">any provision of any primary or derivative legislation shall be deemed also to refer to any modification thereof;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">headings shall be ignored in construing these Platform Rules; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p580 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">e)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">the Annexes form an integral part of these Platform Rules and shall have effect accordingly.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p581 ft125">2. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 2</SPAN></P>
<P class="p582 ft122">INTRODUCTION</P>
<P class="p583 ft5">The Platform is set up by the EIB to administer externally contributed resources that shall be used to facilitate the EIB’s activities across the full range of countries and sectors and using the full range of instruments described in Article 4.6 of these Platform Rules, through the establishment of the respective Funds under the Platform.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">2.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Policy framework</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">Operations supported with the resources contributed to the Funds established under the Platform shall be consistent with the objectives, policies, guidelines and principles, as amended from time to time, applicable to the EIB’s activities, and including, but not limited to, the following:</P>

<P class="p569 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p494 ft31">2.1.1. Main objectives</P>
<P class="p495 ft5">Main objectives include the following:</P>
<P class="p76 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Promoting growth and development in beneficiary countries;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p0 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Supporting the EU enlargement;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p78 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Supporting strategic partnerships and security;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p78 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Reducing and eventually eradicating poverty;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p0 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">e)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Supporting the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals</SPAN><SPAN class="ft41">1</SPAN>;</P>
<P class="p0 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">f)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Development of social and economic infrastructure;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p0 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">g)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Local private sector development;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p0 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">h)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Climate change mitigation and adaptation; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p0 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft124">Regional integration.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft31">2.1.2. Applicable policies, guidelines and principles</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The management of the Platform as well as of the respective Funds established thereunder shall be performed with the application of the EIB’s internal policies and guidelines, such as environmental, social and gender policies, as well as those related to <NOBR>anti-fraud,</NOBR> fight against tax evasion, tax avoidance, harmful tax practices, <NOBR>anti-money</NOBR> laundering and fight against financing of terrorism, market abuse, <NOBR>non-cooperation</NOBR> with <NOBR>non-transparent</NOBR> and uncooperative jurisdictions, procurement and transparency policies<SPAN class="ft41">2</SPAN>.</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">It should be noted that several <NOBR>cross-cutting</NOBR> principles are also applicable to the EIB activities, and consequently shall also be applicable to the operations supported through the resources contributed to the Funds under the Platform, including the following:</P>
<P class="p585 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Protection of human rights and safeguarding against social, climate and environmental risks that should be achieved by ensuring compliance with the EIB’s environmental and social standards, as well as the EIB’s Climate Action Statement;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p586 ft127"><SPAN class="ft27">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft126">Protection of women’s rights that should be achieved through the application of the EIB’s social standards, and the promotion of gender equality and women’s economic empowerment based on the implementation of the EIB Group Gender Equality Strategy;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p587 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Avoiding investments being impacted by, or indeed triggering, conflict, social tensions and violence through the application of a conflict sensitivity approach to operations in fragile, </SPAN><NOBR>conflict-affected</NOBR> or <NOBR>conflict-prone</NOBR> contexts;</P>
<P class="p585 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Ownership that should be ensured through consultations with the beneficiary countries and ensuring the alignment and complementarity of operations with relevant regional, national and local strategies and priorities;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p588 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">e)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft109">Cost-Sharing</SPAN></NOBR> that should be achieved through ensuring that, whenever possible, final beneficiaries shall make an appropriate contribution to the operations financed under the Platform in accordance with modalities to be determined by the Contributors and the Bank;</P>
<P class="p589 ft129"><SPAN class="ft42">1</SPAN><SPAN class="ft128">The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is a set of 17 "Global Goals" with 169 targets between them. Spearheaded by the United Nations through a deliberative process involving its 193 Member States, as well as global civil society, the goals are contained in paragraph 54 United Nations Resolution A/RES/70/1 of 25 September 2015.</SPAN></P>

<P class="p557 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p558 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p591 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">f)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft133">Cost-Efficiency</SPAN></NOBR> that should be achieved by ensuring that only a justifiable proportion of grants/subsidies/guarantees shall be provided along other sources of financing. It shall be ensured that the costs of implementation of the operations shall always be reasonable;</P>
<P class="p592 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">g)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Sustainability that should be achieved by seeking to ensure an improved local capacity by transferring knowledge to final beneficiaries and maintaining the impact of the investment also beyond the life of the operation;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p593 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">h)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Catalytic Impact that should be achieved by ensuring that resources are provided only for activities that can contribute to the subsequent mobilisation of additional funds, partners, or further assistance in supported areas; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p594 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft133">Promotion of open market that should be achieved by ensuring that overcompensation is avoided and that supported operations do not distort the functioning of the market.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p595 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">2.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Expected Results and Impact</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">The following section provides the list of results and describes impact that the operations supported through the resources contributed to the Funds under the Platform are expected to achieve. Such results and impacts include the following:</P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Leverage of the overall investment</SPAN></P>
<P class="p596 ft5">Appropriate leverage may allow to implement investments that would otherwise not take place, to accelerate their implementation, or to increase their chances of success. Through leverage the scope and scale of the overall investment may also be increased to deliver a larger impact than would otherwise be the case, extend the benefits to a wider group of final beneficiaries, especially the poor and vulnerable groups, and boost private sector investments that may otherwise not be engaged.</P>
<P class="p422 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Economic benefits</SPAN></P>
<P class="p597 ft5">Economic benefits include the creation or sustainability of jobs, boost of economic growth, purse of reforms and a transition to a market economy.</P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Financial benefits</SPAN></P>
<P class="p598 ft5">Financial benefits include broadening access to finance to target groups, improvement of financial viability, lowering <NOBR>end-user</NOBR> tariffs.</P>
<P class="p422 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Social benefits</SPAN></P>
<P class="p599 ft5">Social benefits include the limitation of affordability constraints for low income households, economic inclusion and social wellbeing, gender equality, inclusive public consultations.</P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">e)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Environmental impact</SPAN></P>
<P class="p598 ft5">Environmental impact relates to an enhanced consideration of the environmental dimension of the investment and higher environmental standards achieved.</P>
<P class="p600 ft5">15</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p0 ft102">17</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_100">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p568 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p569 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p494 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">f)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft133">Promotion of innovation</SPAN></P>
<P class="p601 ft5">Promotion of innovation includes focus on innovative proposals, which do not necessarily require large amounts of resources but can provide high value added to the beneficiary countries, and operations aimed at supporting vulnerable groups through innovation (e.g. digital technology and financial inclusion of women).</P>
<P class="p422 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">g)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Other benefits</SPAN></P>
<P class="p601 ft5">Other benefits may include positive externalities realised by the operation, which would not happen without the presence of the funding component, including addressing market failures and avoiding market distortions, decentralization and commercialization activities.</P>
<P class="p602 ft125">3. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 3</SPAN></P>
<P class="p603 ft122">THE PLATFORM SET UP</P>
<P class="p495 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">3.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Eligible Contributors</SPAN></P>
<P class="p573 ft5">Any Member State of the European Union as well as the European Commission, and the EFTA Countries can make Contribution(s) to a Fund under the Platform.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Third Party Financing is subject to approval by the EIB and the relevant Fund’s Contributors’ Committee. Third Parties shall enter into a Third Party Agreement with the Bank for the purpose of contributing Third Party Financing to a Fund under the Platform. Unless otherwise provided in these Platform Rules or in Annex I <SPAN class="ft47">“Receipt of Third Party Financing” </SPAN>to these Platform Rules, or unless otherwise agreed by the parties to a Third Party Agreement, these Platform Rules shall apply to each Third Party.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">3.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Contributions</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft31">3.2.1. Legal Framework applicable to Contributions</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">Contribution(s) shall be contributed by each Contributor pursuant to a Contribution Agreement which shall specify the amount of the respective Contribution and its payment schedule.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Objectives to be pursued under each Fund, its indicative budget, as well as eligible operations shall be defined in the Fund Description annexed to the Contribution Agreement.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">By entering into a Contribution Agreement, the Contributor shall be deemed to acknowledge, agree, and undertake to continuously comply with any and all terms and conditions of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p604 ft5">16</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p0 ft102">18</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_101">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p557 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p558 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p494 ft31">3.2.2. Time schedule for Contributions</P>
<P class="p565 ft5">Contributions can be provided at any time during the term of a Fund under the Platform, upon execution of a Contribution Agreement between the Bank and the relevant Contributor and subject to the terms thereof. A Contributor may at any time increase the amount of its Contribution upon the execution of a further Contribution Agreement between the Bank and the Contributor and subject to the terms thereof. The provisions of these Platform Rules relating to Contributions shall apply equally to additional Contributions with respect to that same Fund.</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">By entering into a Contribution Agreement, the Contributor irrevocably and unconditionally undertakes to make the Contribution described therein on the relevant Contribution payment dates, as defined in the Contribution Agreement, and allow the EIB, as the Administrator, to proceed with the allocation of the relevant Contribution Paid, subject to any fees, costs, charges, and losses, to operations according to the scheduled payment dates specified in that Contribution Agreement.</P>
<P class="p495 ft31">3.2.3. Payment of Contributions and Third Party Financing</P>
<P class="p583 ft5">Each Contribution and each Third Party Financing shall be (a) denominated and paid exclusively in euro and (b) paid by the relevant Contributor or Third Party, as the case may be, in accordance with the terms of the applicable Contribution Agreement or Third Party Agreement, in the form of:</P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">a single instalment; or</SPAN></P>
<P class="p580 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">in several instalments as set out in the relevant Contribution Agreement or Third Party Agreement.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p432 ft5">On an exceptional basis specific payment modalities may be defined in the relevant Contribution Agreement or Third Party Agreement.</P>
<P class="p605 ft136">Each Contributor shall transfer the payable Contributions or Third Party Financing directly to the Account or the bank account indicated by the Bank in the relevant Third Party Agreement.</P>
<P class="p3 ft31">3.2.4. Allocation, administration and management of Contributions Paid</P>
<P class="p606 ft5">Each Contributor hereby authorises and appoints the Bank to act as the Administrator of the Platform to:</P>
<P class="p593 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">provide the services described in these Platform Rules and in particular, the allocation (in accordance with Article 5.2 of these Platform Rules) of the Contributions Paid, the administration and the management of the Resources;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">credit the Resources to the relevant Fund Account; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p607 ft138"><SPAN class="ft27">c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft137">debit from the relevant Fund Account any amount (i) to be disbursed for the purpose of the activities of the Platform, (ii) due to the EIB in accordance with the Legal Framework (in particular, Article 7 of these Platform Rules), (iii) repaid to any Contributor,</SPAN></P>
<P class="p608 ft110"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft139">corresponding to any fees, losses, and costs arising out of the treasury management (including, but not limited to, fees, losses, and costs charged by the Unitary Fund), and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p513 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(v)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft140">corresponding to any applicable charge.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p609 ft5">17</P>
</DIV>

<P class="p0 ft102">19</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>

<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p568 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p569 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p570 ft5">The Bank shall ensure that the Contributions Paid are allocated, and the Resources administered and managed with the same diligence as the Bank's own resources and operations and in accordance with the Legal Framework<SPAN class="ft41">3</SPAN>. In particular, the Bank shall promptly upon receipt of the Contributions on the Account, allocate the Contributions to a specific Fund in accordance with the terms of the Contribution Agreement.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Contributions Paid shall, for and in relation to each Fund, be kept in separately and segregated from any and all of the Bank's own resources and from any other Contributions Paid allocated to another Fund or other assets held by the Bank in any capacity. Any cash held on the Account is held at the risk of the Contributors.</P>
<P class="p610 ft110">Each Contributor acknowledges and agrees that the Contributions may be allocated by the Bank on a <NOBR>non-refundable</NOBR> basis, depending on the Instrument used to carry out the operations of an individual Fund, and that a part or all of their Contribution may not be repaid to them. Each Contributor acknowledges and agrees that it is its intention to invest in such Instruments and the Bank shall not be held liable towards the Contributors for the repayment of the Contributions should all or part of these Contributions be invested on a <NOBR>non-refundable</NOBR> basis and each Contributor agrees to hold the Bank harmless in such a situation.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Bank shall report on its administration and management of the Resources to the Contributors in accordance with the provisions of Article 9 of these Platform Rules and with the Legal Framework.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31">3.2.5 Change in status of Contributor</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">If a Contributor changes its status (for example by ceasing to be a Member State of the European Union or an EFTA Country) with the result that, after having become a Contributor, it ceases to fall within the definition of "Contributor" set out in Article 1, it shall nonetheless remain a Contributor with the full rights and privileges of a Contributor. It shall not be a Third Party for the purposes of the Legal Framework and its Contributions shall not be Third Party Financing. This provision shall apply in respect of all Contributions to all Funds under the Platform, whether the applicable Contribution Agreement was signed before or after the change in status of the Contributor.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">3.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Resources under management</SPAN></P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Each Contributor acknowledges and agrees that: (i) any investment carried out by the Bank, including any investment in the Unitary Fund, is subject to fees, losses and costs, which are to be borne by the Resources, and (ii) the amounts available for financing operations through the Funds under the Platform may be lower than the Resources.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Resources shall be managed in accordance with the principles of sound financial management and shall be invested in accordance with Article 8 of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p611 ft27"><SPAN class="ft42">3</SPAN><SPAN class="ft141">For more details refer to Article 12 of these Platform Rules.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p590 ft5">18</P>

<P class="p558 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p494 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">3.4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Transfer of Resources</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">A Fund Outstanding Balance may be partially or fully transferred from one Fund to (an)other Fund(s), and to (an)other Instrument(s), provided that the EIB and the respective Contributor(s), agree on this transfer. In cases where a Fund Outstanding Balance is transferred, partially or totally, from one Fund to another, the Bank shall decide if any charges shall be applied to the transferred Fund outstanding Balance, or a portion thereof, to ensure for the recovery of administrative costs and direct expenses.</P>
<P class="p612 ft125">4. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 4</SPAN></P>
<P class="p613 ft122">FUNDS, ELIGIBLE OPERATIONS AND INSTRUMENTS UNDER THE PLATFORM</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">4.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Creation of a Fund</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">The Bank may establish a new Fund under the Platform at its discretion and may take such a decision on the basis of, among others, the needs and requests of existing or potential Contributors. Each Fund shall be established in accordance with these Platform Rules and any specific rules set out in the relevant Fund Description, as applicable and agreed between the Bank and the relevant Contributor(s).</P>
<P class="p583 ft5">For each Fund created, the Bank shall open a Fund Account and shall operate the respective Contributions Paid in accordance with Article 3.2.4 of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">4.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Operations under the Funds</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">The operations supported through the Contributions made to the Funds under the Platform shall be selected and administered in accordance with the EIB’s mandate and the objectives in all countries where EIB is operational. The Bank shall originate, identify, and structure operations, based on demand from eligible project promoters, in accordance with the eligibility criteria defined in the Fund Description.</P>
<P class="p583 ft5">Such operations can cover a broad geographic and sectorial scope and various types of assistance Instruments, of which a selection shall be made for each Fund.</P>
<P class="p566 ft5">In relation to each Fund under the Platform the eligible regions, countries, sectors, beneficiaries and Instruments shall be specified in the Fund Description.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">4.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Geographical Coverage</SPAN></P>
<P class="p614 ft110">All countries in which the EIB is mandated to operate in are eligible for financial support from Contributions made to the Funds under the Platform, both within and outside of the EU<SPAN class="ft142">4</SPAN>.</P>
<P class="p615 ft27"><SPAN class="ft130">4 </SPAN>The information about eligible countries is available on the EIB Website: <SPAN class="ft131">http://www.eib.europa.eu/projects/regions/index.htm</SPAN></P>
<P class="p616 ft5">19</P>
</DIV>

<P class="p0 ft102">21</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_104">

<P class="p568 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p569 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p494 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">4.4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Eligible Sectors</SPAN></P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Legal activities in all economic sectors are eligible for financial support from Funds under the Platform, with the exclusion of activities with a negative social or environmental impact, not addressed by mitigation plans approved by the competent authorities and specifically excluded from EIB lending, as per the EIB internal procedures<SPAN class="ft41">5</SPAN>. Sector coverage shall duly take into consideration the relevant EU regional and country strategies.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">4.5.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Beneficiaries</SPAN></P>
<P class="p617 ft5">Typical beneficiaries of the funding provided under the Platform shall be both public and private sector entities such as:</P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">states and other public sector entities;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p401 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">public enterprises managed in accordance with market principles;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p618 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">financial intermediaries such as commercial banks, financial institutions, private equity funds and </SPAN><NOBR>micro-finance</NOBR> institutions;</P>
<P class="p619 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">local and/or foreign private enterprises (large enterprises, project finance vehicles, SMEs and </SPAN><NOBR>mid-caps);</NOBR> and</P>
<P class="p197 ft145"><SPAN class="ft143">(v)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft144">non-governmental</SPAN></NOBR> organisations.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">4.6.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Instruments</SPAN></P>
<P class="p620 ft5">The following Instruments may be deployed within the Funds under the Platform (the below list is not exhaustive and may be updated unilaterally by the Bank from time to time):</P>
<P class="p585 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft146">Technical assistance: </SPAN>an instrument aimed at supporting preparation and implementation of investments through institutional capacity building and the financing of e.g. <NOBR>pre-feasibility</NOBR> and feasibility studies, design and tender documents, institutional and legal appraisals, environmental and social impact assessments, project management, as well as financing upstream studies, gender analysis or advisory services to beneficiaries.</P>
<P class="p621 ft138"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft147">Investment grants</SPAN>: <NOBR>non-reimbursable</NOBR> contribution to finance tangible or intangible components of an infrastructure project or venture, in joint or parallel <NOBR>co-financing</NOBR> with financing from other investors. In particular, the investment grants may decrease the investment costs for a beneficiary through financing a part of the investment or through an increase of the concessionality of the financing package of a given project. They may also target specific project components which have substantial demonstrable social or environmental benefits or which can mitigate negative environmental or social impacts.</P>
<P class="p622 ft138"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft148">Interest rate subsidies: </SPAN>the provision of a grant amount to an investor financing an operation to enable it to make <NOBR>long-term</NOBR> finance available in flexible ways that reduce the total amount of debt service to be paid by the borrower. Such subsidies can therefore</P>
<P class="p623 ft27"><SPAN class="ft130">5 </SPAN>The list of "Excluded Activities" is available on the EIB Website: <NOBR><SPAN class="ft131">http://www.eib.org/about/documents/excluded-activities-2013.htm</SPAN></NOBR></P>
<P class="p624 ft5">20</P>

<P class="p558 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p625 ft5">be applied upfront or over time. In either case, such grants should aim to minimise market distortions. Financing operations benefiting from interest rate subsidies shall be in line with the EU position on debt sustainability in low income countries, where applicable.</P>
<P class="p593 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft149">Financial instruments</SPAN>: including but not limited to guarantees (including loan guarantee cost financing and insurance premia), equity or <NOBR>quasi-equity</NOBR> investments or participations, and <NOBR>risk-sharing</NOBR> instruments.</P>
<P class="p561 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(v)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft150">Direct exchange: </SPAN>focused on strengthening the capacity of public and private sector organisations and groups via secondments, internships, and other activities which increase their knowledge, skill level and/or efficiency.</P>
<P class="p626 ft125">5. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 5</SPAN></P>
<P class="p627 ft122">GOVERNANCE OF THE PLATFORM</P>
<P class="p495 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">5.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Governance structure</SPAN></P>
<P class="p422 ft5">The Governance structure of the Platform shall consist of:</P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">the Administrator;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p3 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Partnerships Committees at Platform level; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p401 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">Contributors’ Committee at Fund level.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">5.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Administrator</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">The Administrator shall receive Contributions Paid and manage the respective Resources (including the management of the Fund Outstanding Balance), in accordance with the Legal Framework and the Bank’s policies and procedures applicable to the administration of the assets stemming from the Contributions Paid.</P>
<P class="p566 ft5">The Administrator is responsible for ensuring that operations supported under each Fund under the Platform are compliant with the Fund Description for that Fund and with these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p422 ft5">Roles and responsibilities of the Administrator include the following:</P>
<P class="p578 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">administering Eligible Operations, including entering into agreements with beneficiaries, where appropriate;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">preparing documents for the Bank’s Governing Bodies’ approval;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p578 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft151">organizing meetings of each Contributors’ Committee and of the Partnerships Committees;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p628 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">preparing and circulating minutes of meetings of the Contributors and Partnerships Committees;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p629 ft5">21</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p0 ft102">23</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_106">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p568 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p569 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p494 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(v)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">handling written procedures in accordance with Article 5.8 of these Platform Rules;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p585 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(vi)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft151">compiling progress reports of operations and financial statements for distribution to each Contributors’ Committee; preparing the Platform’s annual Contributors’ report and other relevant documents necessary to allow the Partnerships Committee and each Contributors’ Committee to carry out their respective duties;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p630 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(vii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft152">informing each Contributors’ Committee about operations and activities financed from Third Party Financing;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p631 ft5"><SPAN class="ft28">(viii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft153">providing guidance on the functioning of Platform and the underlying Fund processes and requirements;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p631 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(ix)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">preparing proposed amendments to the Fund Description of a specific Fund for decision by the Contributors’ Committee;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p631 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(x)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">proposing amendments to the provisions of the Platform Rules, in consultation with Contributors, where appropriate;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(xi)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft151">supporting each Contributors’ Committee in commissioning reviews and evaluations;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p588 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(xii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft152">ensuring that, in communicating internally and externally, in its publications, in communication with beneficiaries, countries and other entities as well as the media, appropriate visibility is given to the Platform and its Contributors;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p585 ft5"><SPAN class="ft28">(xiii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft153">carrying out such other functions as may be necessary for the efficient administration of the Platform and the Funds created thereunder, except for functions which pertain to the competence of the relevant Contributors’ Committee and which have not been delegated to the Bank; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p631 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(xiv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft154">liaising and coordinating, to the extent necessary to fulfil its role, with Contributors and other relevant parties.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p632 ft110">The Bank, as Administrator, operates in accordance with applicable EIB policies and procedures. It is accountable to the Contributors’ Committees for the performance of its obligations in accordance with Article 12 of these Platform Rules, and is serving as the liaison between the Contributors’ Committees and the respective departments at the Bank. In this respect, the Administrator handles Funds’ operations in accordance with the EIB’s Access to</P>
<P class="p574 ft5">Information Policy available on the website of the Bank <SPAN class="ft155">http://www.eib.org/attachments/strategies/pai_ips_en.pdf</SPAN>.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">5.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Partnerships Committees</SPAN></P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Contributors to the Funds shall be invited to meetings of the Partnerships Committees as organised from time to time at the Platform level for thematic and geographical windows, to discuss and provide strategic guidance to the EIB, advise on the operation of the Platform and on the opportunity to create new Funds.</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">The Partnerships Committee is solely an advisory body with no decision making power in relation to either the Platform or any Fund under the Platform.</P>
<P class="p633 ft5">22</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p0 ft102">24</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_107">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p557 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p558 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p494 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">5.4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Contributors’ Committees</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">For each Fund under the Platform a Contributors’ Committee shall be set up. The main role of each Contributors’ Committee is to oversee activities under the respective Fund and to approve specific operations supported through the Contributions made to such Fund. Decisions of each Contributors’ Committee on operations shall be made either by tacit procedure or during meetings, as further described in Article 5.8 of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p422 ft5">The roles and responsibilities of the Contributors’ Committee include the following:</P>
<P class="p580 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">approving proposed operations within 15 Business Days of their receipt on a tacit basis, as applicable in accordance with Article 5.8 of these Platform Rules;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p197 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">approving Third Party Financing;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p634 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">approving redemption (to the Contributors) or reallocation (to another Fund) of remaining Contributions Paid in the relevant Fund upon its termination;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p635 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft113">approving any amendment to the Fund Description, including any prolongation of the Fund;</SPAN></P>

<P class="p191 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">5.5.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Members of the Partnerships Committees and the Contributors’ Committees</SPAN></P>
<P class="p577 ft5">Each Contributor to a Fund is entitled to designate a member that shall represent such Contributor in the Partnerships Committee and the Contributors Committees. The Bank shall also be represented in the Partnerships Committee and in each of the Contributors’ Committees. Unless otherwise decided by the Bank and the Contributors Committees, Third Party Financing pursuant to Article 3.1 of these Platform Rules does not entitle the respective Third Parties to be represented in the Partnerships Committees and the relevant Contributors’ Committee and to attend their meetings.</P>
<P class="p639 ft110">Contributors shall each appoint a member and an alternate member (the later only participating in a meeting in the case of absence of the member) and communicate in writing their names and contact details to the Bank within 30 Business Days following the execution of the Contribution Agreement. Each Contributor shall inform the Bank about a replacement of a member or an alternate within 30 Business Days of their appointment. Both the member and the alternate shall be authorised to exercise the Contributor’s rights in the Partnerships Committees and in each of the Contributors’ Committees. The member or the alternate, in the absence of the member, may be accompanied by no more than one advisory staff.</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">An individual may at the same time serve as a member or an alternate of more than one Contributor in the Partnerships Committees and/or each relevant Contributors’ Committee</P>

<P class="p494 ft5">subject to the <NOBR>non-objection</NOBR> of the Bank.</P>
<P class="p495 ft5">No voting rights shall be granted to other persons than the designated members and alternates.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The number of the Bank’s representatives attending the meeting of the Partnerships Committee and the Contributors’ Committees shall not be limited.</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">If the European Commission becomes a Contributor to any of the Funds under the Platform, it shall be treated, for the purposes of these Platform Rules, as any other Contributor.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Each Partnerships Committee and each Contributors’ Committee shall have a chairperson appointed by the EIB within 15 Business Days prior to the first scheduled meeting of such Partnerships Committee and each Contributors’ Committee or prior to the submission of first proposals for decision by the tacit procedure, as applicable. Such an appointment shall be communicated by the EIB to all the Contributors. A chairperson may be replaced by the EIB at its sole discretion at any time. The chairperson may invite representatives of governments, other institutions and entities to attend specific agenda items of meetings of the Partnerships Committees or the Contributors’ Committees as observers.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">5.6.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Meetings and conferences</SPAN></P>
<P class="p573 ft5">Meetings of the Partnerships Committees and the Contributors’ Committees that may take place from time to time shall be organised in the Bank’s headquarters in Luxembourg, or in such other place as may be indicated by the Bank.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">It is foreseen that an annual conference shall be organised once per annum, open for all Contributors and aimed at promoting the activities under the Funds and creating an opportunity for <NOBR>fund-raising.</NOBR></P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Concurrently with such an annual conference, the Partnerships Committees shall meet within thematic and geographical windows, with the aim to discussing and advising on strategic issues, overall orientations and priorities. Contributors Committees shall meet on a needs be basis either physically or via video conference.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">5.7.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Convening power</SPAN></P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The chairperson of each Contributors’ Committee may convene meetings at any time at his own initiative or if so decided in a previous meeting of the Contributors’ Committee, or at the request of the Contributors to the relevant Fund, whose Contributions Paid account for not less than <NOBR>one-third</NOBR> of the aggregate amount of all Contributions Paid in the relevant Fund. The Contributors’ Committees may conduct business electronically via email or with the use of other devices or services that may be indicated by the Bank and made available to the Contributors.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">5.8.</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft135">Decision-making</SPAN></NOBR> process</P>
<P class="p617 ft5">Unless otherwise agreed in the Fund Description, decisions of the Contributors’ Committees are made as follows:</P>

<P class="p591 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">during meetings, audioor video conference meetings. Decisions taken during meetings are deemed binding if adopted by consensus. If no consensus can be reached, decisions can only be approved by Contributors representing at least:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p641 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft156">2/3 of the total amount of the Contributions Paid actually received by the Bank since the inception of the Fund from the Contributors present or represented at such a meeting; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p642 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft114">one-half</SPAN></NOBR> plus one of the total number of Contributors to the Fund;</P>
<P class="p495 ft5">or</P>
<P class="p559 ft110"><SPAN class="ft27">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft157">in writing, through a tacit procedure where the Contributors shall be given 15 Business Days to vote following the receipt of the draft decision and the corresponding documents. Written procedure requests may be submitted, with corresponding documentation, at any time. Such requests are deemed approved unless Contributors representing more than 1/3 of the total amount of the Contributions Paid to the Fund reject the proposed decision. The Chairperson shall inform the members and alternates of each Contributors’ Committees of the respective outcome of the written procedure at</SPAN></P>

Rejected decision by way of written procedure shall be discussed at the next meeting of the Contributors’ Committee. In exceptional circumstances, the 15 Business Days period for tacit approval may be shortened by the chairperson in duly justified cases but in any case shall not be shorter than 5 Business Days.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">In relation to each Fund, Contributors representing not less than (i) <NOBR>one-half</NOBR> plus one, of the Contributors who have entered into a Contribution Agreement with the Bank relating to that Fund and (ii) <NOBR>one-half</NOBR> plus 1% of the aggregate amount of all Contributions Paid in relation to that Fund since its inception, shall constitute a quorum at meetings of the relevant Contributors’ Committee.</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">Representatives and alternates shall notify the Bank in writing of any comments or requests for further information and of any potential conflict of interest with regard to one or more points on the agenda, at least 5 Business Days before the date of the meeting. They shall withdraw from the voting on the items in case of which the potential conflict of interest has been identified.</P>
<P class="p566 ft5">If a Contributor identifies that it has a potential conflict of interest in relation to a request for a decision to be taken by written procedure, it shall inform the chairperson of that potential conflict of interest. The chairperson shall decide whether or not the Contributor in question shall be permitted to vote on the written procedure and may decide that the decision must be submitted to a meeting of Contributors.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">5.9.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Agenda and documentation</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">Prior to any meeting of the Contributors’ Committee, the Administrator shall prepare an agenda and relevant documentation and provide them to each Contributor’s designated member and alternate in electronic form 15 Business Days prior to the meeting.</P>

<P class="p494 ft31">5.10. Minutes and disclosures</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Issues discussed during the Contributors’ Committee meeting and decisions made shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting prepared by the Administrator. Draft minutes are circulated by the Administrator within 30 Business Days after the meeting to each member and alternate, for approval and/or comments, if any. Should amendments be requested by Contributors, the Administrator shall prepare and distribute final minutes for approval within 15 Business Days to all members and alternates of the Contributors’ Committee.</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">In case of disagreements that cannot be resolved, the proposed amendment to the minutes shall be annexed to the minutes. The minutes shall, as a minimum, state the time and venue of the meeting, as well as the participants, the proceedings and the decisions adopted. If a decision is not unanimous, it shall be stated who voted for and who voted against. Minutes shall be signed by the Chairman. Minutes, shall, unless the contrary is proved, be conclusive evidence of the proceedings at a meeting.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">5.11. Correspondence</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Correspondence concerning the meetings shall be addressed to the Administrator. All notices, correspondence or documents to be transmitted pursuant to these Platform Rules may be transmitted using electronic mail or delivered via standard mail.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31">5.12. Confidentiality</P>
<P class="p632 ft5">Any persons attending Partnerships or Contributors’ Committees’ meetings shall be required to observe the confidentiality of the Committees’ work and deliberations. They shall not divulge any confidential information coming to their knowledge during the performance of their duties to persons outside the Bank or the Partnerships or Contributors’ Committees other than to persons assisting them in the performance of their duties, provided that such persons are subject to the equivalent duty of confidentiality. Documents relating to such work and deliberations shall be for the use of those to whom they are addressed, who shall be responsible for their safekeeping and the preservation of their confidentiality.</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">The minutes of meetings of Contributors, and decisions taken by written procedure, shall be considered confidential; however, the Bank or the chairperson of any Contributors’ Committee may publish or disclose decisions taken by the Contributors.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">5.13. Remuneration</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Contributors do not receive remuneration and shall cover their own costs of participation unless otherwise decided in relation to any Fund by the Contributors of that Fund.</P>

<P class="p645 ft125">6. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 6</SPAN></P>
<P class="p646 ft122">APPROVAL PROCESS OF OPERATIONS</P>
<P class="p495 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">6.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Design and implementation of operations</SPAN></P>
<P class="p583 ft5">In order to ensure the quality of operations, the Bank shall make available Bank’s staff that will provide project expertise and high professional capacity and carry out the processes necessary to establish, implement and administer the operations efficiently.</P>
<P class="p566 ft5">The Bank shall ensure that projects submitted for financing are technically, economically and financially viable. All projects undergo an <NOBR>ex-ante</NOBR> due diligence performed by sector experts and are monitored on a regular basis according to the Bank’s monitoring procedures and guidelines.</P>
<P class="p639 ft110">Implementation is embedded into the different Bank departments, and the EIB staff includes, among others, loan officers, financial monitoring officers, sector specialists in charge of the design and monitoring of the technical substance of the project as well as providing oversight of climate, social and environmental considerations including gender equality, procurement, legal, financial and other issues as deemed necessary. The EIB external/local offices are also involved in all steps of the operation cycle as necessary. In addition, corporate secretariat officers shall ensure the efficient <NOBR>decision-making</NOBR> process for operational and other documents submitted to the Partnerships Committees and the Contributors Committees.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">6.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Submission of operations for approval</SPAN></P>
<P class="p647 ft5">No operation may be submitted to the Contributors of any Fund for approval unless it has first been approved by the Governing Bodies of the Bank.</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">Operations cannot be presented for approval in relation to a specific Fund if the total of all Contributions Paid in respect of that Fund (including Third Party Financing, as applicable) is lower than the amount necessary to finance the operation, after deduction of actual disbursements, existing commitments and administrative fees.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">6.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Operations below a defined threshold</SPAN></P>
<P class="p565 ft5">Unless otherwise agreed in the Fund Description, for operations financed from a Fund up to a certain threshold to be defined for each Fund in the relevant Fund Description, the Contributors’ Committee fully delegates the authority for approving the allocation of Contributions Paid to the Bank’s Governing Bodies. The Bank’s Governing Bodies’ decision on the allocation of Contributions Paid shall be guided by the eligibility criteria set out in the Fund Description.</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">Operations approved by the Bank’s Governing Bodies shall be communicated, for information, to each member and alternate of the Contributors’ Committee within 15 Business Days following the Bank’s Governing Bodies’ approval.</P>
<P class="p648 ft5">27</P>

<P class="p494 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">6.4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Operations above a defined threshold</SPAN></P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Unless otherwise agreed in the Fund Description, for operations above the threshold defined for each Fund, in addition to and subsequently to the Bank’s Governing Bodies’ approval, the Contributors’ Committee shall be responsible for approving the allocation of Contributions Paid, in accordance with the <NOBR>decision-making</NOBR> process described in Article 5.8 of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">6.5.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Approved operations</SPAN></P>
<P class="p573 ft5">Eligible Operations shall be placed on the list of the Eligible Operations managed by the Administrator.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">An approval of an operation remains valid for 24 months. If the relevant operation has not been signed by that time, the approval shall lapse unless prolonged for one or more additional periods of up to 12 months (provided that the effect of the extensions does not prolong the authorisation to more than four years from the date of the Bank’s Governing Bodies’ approval of the operation) by either (i) the Bank alone if the total amount of the considered operation does not exceed the threshold referred to in Article 6.3 of these Platform Rules or (ii) the Bank together with the Contributors’ Committee (using the <NOBR>non-objection</NOBR> procedure) if the total amount of the considered operation exceeds the threshold referred to in Article 6.4 of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p649 ft125">7. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 7</SPAN></P>
<P class="p650 ft122">FEES</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Bank shall apply a fee structured to cover both: (i) costs incurred in administering the Platform and all the Funds under the Platform; and (ii) costs associated with implementing different types of Instruments under the Funds. The amount of fees owed to the Bank shall be deducted directly from the Fund Account.</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">Unless otherwise agreed in the Fund Description, the fees charged to Contributors shall be the following:</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">7.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Administration fee</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5">Administration fee shall be calculated as follows:</P>
<P class="p651 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">1 percent on the total committed Contribution, to be deducted by the Bank from the first instalment of such total committed Contribution; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p652 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">0.25 percent per annum, calculated at the Platform level</SPAN><SPAN class="ft41">6 </SPAN>on the outstanding available funds as at 31 December of the relevant year, to be deducted by the Bank within one month after the end of the financial year. The amount of the management fees charged with respect to the management of any pooled</P>
<P class="p653 ft28"><SPAN class="ft158">6</SPAN><SPAN class="ft159">For the avoidance of doubt, “calculated at the Platform level” means that the fee of 0.25% shall be calculated on the Fund Outstanding Balance for each Fund as at 31 December of the relevant year and deducted from the cumulative Contributions paid in by each Contributor to each Fund.</SPAN></P>

<P class="p656 ft110">The Administration fee covers activities carried out to raise or access Contributors’ funds, account for the use of funds (audits, evaluations), management of Fund Outstanding Balances (such as costs arising from cash accounts, calculation agents, custody fees), communication and Contributor visibility, creation and maintenance of dedicated IT systems, Contributors engagement and all other costs to meet obligations placed on the Bank by Contributors.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">7.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Instrument fee</SPAN><SPAN class="ft160">7</SPAN></P>
<P class="p606 ft5">Instrument fee shall be payable upon the approval of a given operation under the Fund, as follows:</P>
<P class="p642 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Investment grants and interest rate subsidies: 1 percent;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p657 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft151">Technical assistance: 3.5 percent; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p658 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft107">Financial instruments: 4.5 percent.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">Instrument fee covers the costs of the activity of multiple teams across the Bank contributing to various stages of the instrument management cycle, including the design of operations, the operations approval process, procurement, implementation and monitoring of operations, results and financial reporting, and other operational costs.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">7.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Other fees</SPAN></P>
<P class="p583 ft5">For any additional request by a Contributor beyond those specified in these Platform Rules or in the Fund Description, additional fees may be applied by the Bank to the requesting Contributor.</P>
<P class="p626 ft125">8. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 8</SPAN></P>
<P class="p659 ft122">MANAGEMENT OF OUTSTANDING BALANCE</P>
<P class="p495 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">8.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Investment of Fund Outstanding Balance</SPAN></P>
<P class="p660 ft110">Each Contributor authorises the Bank to invest, at its discretion and at the risk of that Contributor, the Fund Outstanding Balance <NOBR>(pro-rata</NOBR> its Contribution Paid) in accordance with:</P>
<P class="p661 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft156">the Asset Management Guidelines of the EIB (Annex II </SPAN><SPAN class="ft47">“Asset Management Guidelines” </SPAN>to these Platform Rules), where the Platform Outstanding Balance is at least equal to 100,000,000 euros and an investment horizon of more than one year; or</P>
<P class="p662 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">the Unitary Fund in case where the Platform Outstanding Balance is lower than 100,000,000 euros or the investment horizon is less than one year. The Deed</SPAN></P>

<P class="p663 ft5">Poll and the Information Memorandum of the Unitary Fund shall be submitted to each Contributor upon the Bank receiving the Contribution and, as the case may be, upon revision of these documents.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Bank shall be entitled to invest the Platform Outstanding Balance in the Unitary Fund in accordance with this Article 8.1, and to divest the investments in the Unitary Fund any time as necessary to implement an operation. For that purpose, each Contributor hereby authorises the Bank to sign and execute the relevant subscription and redemption forms on its behalf and to deduct any amount concerning subscriptions, and fees and costs charged by the Unitary Fund from the Platform Outstanding Balance.</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">The Contributors shall not interfere in the decision of the Bank to invest the Fund’s Outstanding Balance in accordance with the Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">8.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Proceeds/losses from placement of Fund Outstanding Balance</SPAN></P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Such investments made from the Fund Outstanding Balance may lead to gains or losses and such gains or losses shall be borne by each Fund from which the associated investments were made.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">8.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Investment tools and features</SPAN></P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The details of each investment tool and features available to the Bank in relation to Article 8.1 of these Platform Rules are set out in Annex II <SPAN class="ft47">“Asset Management Guidelines” </SPAN>to these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">8.4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Liability arising from management of Fund Outstanding Balance</SPAN></P>
<P class="p610 ft110">The Bank shall only be bound to use its best endeavours (“<SPAN class="ft161">obligation de moyens”) </SPAN>when carrying out its duties as manager of the Fund’s Outstanding Balance, which each Contributor expressly accepts. The Bank shall in any case only be liable towards the Contributor in case of gross negligence (<SPAN class="ft161">“faute lourde”</SPAN>) or wilful misconduct (<SPAN class="ft161">“faute dolosive”</SPAN>).</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Each Contributor is solely responsible for the transactions made on its behalf by the Bank in accordance with Article 8.1 of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">With regard to the assessment and evaluation of the possible performance and risks of an asset, the Bank’s liability is limited to gross negligence (<SPAN class="ft47">“faute lourde”</SPAN>); this shall also apply to secondary contractual obligations. <P class="p422 ft5">Each Contributor agrees that the Bank does not guarantee any specific results and/or profits.</P>
<P class="p632 ft136">Moreover, the Bank shall not be liable for any losses in the value of the Fund Outstanding Balance resulting from market fluctuations, from changes in the exchange rates or from any other reason, for fluctuations in the yield, for temporary overexposure of the Fund Outstanding</P>

<P class="p626 ft125">9. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 9</SPAN></P>
<P class="p664 ft122">ACCOUNTING AND REPORTING</P>
<P class="p3 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">9.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Accounts</SPAN></P>
<P class="p432 ft5">The Bank shall maintain its recordings in the relevant accounts of the Platform exclusively in euros.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">9.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Financial statements</SPAN></P>
<P class="p605 ft127">The Bank shall prepare the annual audited and consolidated financial statements for the Platform in euros. The consolidated financial statements shall be drawn up on the basis of cash</P>

<P class="p665 ft5">receipts and disbursements except for the investments of Fund Outstanding Balances which shall be reported on a fair value basis.</P>
<P class="p495 ft5">The financial statements shall comprise:</P>
<P class="p651 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">a consolidated statement of account movements of the Funds under the Platform; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p666 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">individual statements for each Fund including the breakdown of all movements with value dates and including an overview of the Fund Outstanding Balances and an overview of fees charged.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5">The financial year of each Fund is the calendar year.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Once they have been audited in accordance with Article 10 of these Platform Rules, the financial statements shall be approved, in line with financial statement approval procedures generally applied by EIB to third party mandates.</P>
<P class="p93 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">9.3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft135">Valuation</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">9.3.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft162">Currencies</SPAN></P>
<P class="p573 ft5">Whenever it shall be necessary for purposes of preparation or presentation of financial statements to determine the value of any currency in terms of another currency, the valuation shall be made by the Bank, using the same principles as the Bank applies for its own resources operations.</P>
<P class="p495 ft31">9.3.2. Investment of Fund Outstanding Balance</P>
<P class="p632 ft110">Whenever it shall be necessary for purposes of preparation or presentation of financial statements to determine the fair value of investments of the Fund or the Platform Outstanding Balance in comparison to the cost of investments, the valuation shall be made by the Bank, using the same principles as the Bank applies for its own resources operations.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">9.4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft123">Reporting</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5">The Bank shall provide each Contributor with the following reports:</P>
<P class="p495 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">9.4.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft162">Reporting at the Fund level:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p652 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">annual operations progress reports: providing a status update on operations, summary of operational highlights and issues over the reporting period, results report on the Fund level and financial status;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p667 ft27"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft163">bi-annual</SPAN></NOBR> operations progress update: providing information on new operations approved, financial resources and disbursements status, and the project pipeline;</P>
<P class="p668 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">operations completion reports: providing a </SPAN><NOBR>fully-fledged</NOBR> information on operation including results and financial aspects; and</P>
<P class="p658 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft113">annual audited and consolidated financial statements.</SPAN></P>

Such Results Framework, which may be revised by the Bank from time to time in consultation with the Contributors, shall be used for reporting and evaluation purposes.</P>
<P class="p583 ft5">In addition, qualitative information shall be provided on important aspects of, among others, sustainability, ownership, broader economic impact, as frequent as appropriate.</P>
<P class="p565 ft5">Limited additional reporting may be agreed with any Contributor to a Fund on a bilateral basis and may be subject to extra fees.</P>
<P class="p495 ft31">9.4.2. Reporting at the Platform level</P>
<P class="p566 ft5">The EIB shall issue a consolidated Annual Contributors Report that shall highlight activities and achievements across the Bank’s Funds portfolio, providing visibility to the Contributors and each of the Funds to which they contribute.</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">In the context of review of the Platform activities (and for the first time in December 2022), the Bank shall provide the Contributors with an evaluation report analysing the impact of operations financed by the Funds under the Platform in the beneficiary countries.</P>
<P class="p669 ft125">10. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 10</SPAN></P>
<P class="p670 ft122">AUDIT AND CONTROL</P>
<P class="p495 ft31">10.1. Audit</P>
<P class="p606 ft5">The consolidated financial statements with respect to the Platform shall be subject to external auditing and the costs of such audit shall be borne by the Platform.</P>
<P class="p660 ft110">The individual Fund Instrument account statements shall not be subject to external audit but shall be covered under the external audit of the Platform’s consolidated financial statements.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">10.2. Control</P>
<P class="p671 ft5">The Platform shall be managed in accordance with the Bank’s usual criteria and procedures, including appropriate control measures.</P>
<P class="p672 ft28"><SPAN class="ft158">[1]</SPAN><SPAN class="ft43">The Bank measures the results of its operations through the 3 PA and ReM frameworks (inside and outside the EU respectively) and the logical framework covers both lending and technical assistance operations. These are based on a 3 pillar methodology, which is designed to show how EIB inputs (e.g. loan, technical advice) generate outputs (e.g. an electricity transmission line, a training programme), which enable outcomes (e.g. improved access to energy, improved institutional capacity) and, over time, lead to impact (e.g. development of economic infrastructure, regional integration).</SPAN></P>

<P class="p674 ft125">11. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 11 DURATION</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft31">11.1. Termination of a Fund and of the Platform</P>
<P class="p620 ft5">The Platform and the Funds under the Platform shall remain in force so long as there remain funds, commitments or investments with respect to the Platform and the Funds.</P>
<P class="p422 ft5">Individual Funds shall not specify a termination date but may be terminated at any time by</P>
<P class="p675 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">a</SPAN><SPAN class="ft164">decision of the relevant Fund’s Contributors’ Committee made with the unanimous consent of the Contributors and, if appropriate, after consultation of the EIB’s Governing Bodies.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p73 ft31">11.2. Payment of the Fund Outstanding Balance upon termination of a Fund</P>
<P class="p676 ft5">Upon a decision of the relevant Contributors’ Committee, in view of the termination of a Fund, the following provisions shall apply with respect to the Fund Outstanding Balance of that Fund:</P>
<P class="p588 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">the Bank shall forthwith cease all activities relating to such corresponding amounts, except those incidental to the orderly realisation, conservation and preservation of such amounts and the settlement of the direct or contingent obligations to which they may be subject;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p677 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">in case where the Fund Outstanding Balance is positive, the Bank shall discuss with Contributors as to possible uses of the funds available from the Fund Outstanding Balance and not yet committed into an operation at the time of termination, with a view to integrate such funds in other Funds or as otherwise agreed with the Contributors. The remaining funds, if any, may as well be returned to the Contributors, if so requested in the decision on termination of the Fund;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p588 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">the Bank shall establish individual Fund Instrument account statements for the Fund being terminated for covering the period from the last annual consolidated financial statements till the date of termination, which shall be subject to the audit procedure referred to in Article 10 of these Platform Rules; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p585 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft113">in case where the Fund Outstanding Balance is equal to zero, the Bank may send to the Contributors an invoice corresponding to any remaining costs incurred, </SPAN><NOBR>pro-rata</NOBR> their respective Contributions Paid.</P>
<P class="p678 ft166">12. <SPAN class="ft165">ARTICLE 12</SPAN></P>
<P class="p679 ft122">STANDARD OF CARE AND LIABILITY</P>
<P class="p422 ft31">12.1. Standard of Care</P>
<P class="p632 ft110">The Bank shall, in accordance with its internal policies and procedures, take all appropriate measures to prevent corrupt, fraudulent, collusive, coercive and obstructive practices in connection with the use of the Funds’ proceeds, and include provisions in its agreements with beneficiaries to give full effect to the relevant Bank guidelines on tax fraud, tax evasion, tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning, money laundering and financing of terrorism.</P>

<P class="p681 ft31">12.2. The Bank acting as for its own resources and operations</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">When acting as Administrator of the Platform, the Bank shall exercise the same degree of care and diligence as for its own resources and operations. Each Contributor acknowledges and agrees that the obligations of the Bank, as Administrator, are to be performed on a best endeavour basis only (<SPAN class="ft47">“obligation de moyens”</SPAN>).</P>
<P class="p565 ft5">The Bank shall administer the Platform as it deems appropriate, in all respects in accordance with these Platform Rules and its internal policies and procedures. The relevant policies and procedures are available on the website of the Bank.</P>
<P class="p565 ft5">The Bank may adopt new internal procedures and policies as it deems appropriate, which shall be applicable to these Platform Rules to the extent compatible with them.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">12.3. The Bank acting in specific circumstances</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">In certain circumstances, the Bank may, with the relevant Contributors’ approval expressed in a form separately agreed upon by the Bank and the relevant Contributor, carry out operations, under an individual Fund, that present a level of risk that can normally not be undertaken and borne by the EIB with its own resources. Therefore, the internal policies and procedures of the Bank shall not apply to these operations.</P>
<P class="p566 ft5">In these specific circumstances, the Bank shall implement ad hoc policies and procedures in accordance with the level of risk inherent to, and the nature of, the contemplated operations. Such ad hoc policies shall always be consistent with the relevant Bank’s guidelines on tax fraud, tax evasion, tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning, money laundering and financing of terrorism.</P>
<P class="p682 ft110">The Bank shall communicate those ad hoc policies and procedures to the relevant Contributors to the extent practically possible before the holding of a Contributors’ Committee to decide on the contemplated operation, as the case may be and, if not practically possible, promptly after the decision to launch the contemplated operation has been made.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">12.4. Liability limited to gross negligence and wilful misconduct</P>
<P class="p566 ft5">Unless otherwise provided for in these Platform Rules and or in the relevant Contribution Agreement, the Bank shall only be liable in the case of gross negligence (<SPAN class="ft47">“faute lourde”</SPAN>) or wilful misconduct (<SPAN class="ft47">“faute dolosive”</SPAN>).</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">12.5. Force majeure and disturbance of business</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">The Bank shall not be liable for any losses caused by abnormal or unforeseeable circumstances, force majeure, riot, war or natural events or due to other occurrences which are beyond the control of the Bank (for instance, strike, <NOBR>lock-out,</NOBR> traffic <NOBR>hold-ups,</NOBR> administrative acts of domestic or foreign authorities or courts, as well as interruptions of telecommunications system or other similar events).</P>

<P class="p494 ft31">12.6. Delays</P>
<P class="p683 ft5">Nothing in these Platform Rules shall require the Bank to take any action which, in the opinion of the Bank acting in good faith, is not possible or would be in contravention of any applicable law, regulation, market custom or practice.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Bank shall not be liable for any delays in the performance of its obligations under these Platform Rules arising from compliance with duties flowing from applicable laws and regulations.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31">12.7. Limited recourse</P>
<P class="p684 ft110">Each Contributor acknowledges and accepts that it has only recourse to the Contributions Paid allocated to the relevant Fund, in accordance with the account statement to be established by the Bank in relation to each Fund and subject to the deduction of any applicable fees, costs, losses, and charges. Each Contributor expressly acknowledges and accepts that once all the Contributions Paid of the relevant Fund have been realised (that is, if upon termination of the relevant Fund, all the Contributions Paid, subject to the deduction of any applicable fees, costs, losses, and charges, have been redeemed on a pro rata basis), it is not entitled to take any further steps against the Bank to recover any further sums due (if any) and the right to receive any such sum shall be extinguished. Each Contributor accepts not to attach or otherwise seize the assets of the Fund, if at all possible.</P>
<P class="p685 ft125">13. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 13</SPAN></P>
<P class="p686 ft122">AMENDMENTS AND ORDER OF PRECEDENCE</P>
<P class="p495 ft31">13.1. Amendments</P>
<P class="p573 ft5">The Bank may, at any time and in consultation with Contributors, amend the provisions of these Platform Rules. The Bank shall inform the Contributors indicating the provisions it intends to modify or add as well as the content thereof. In proposing amendments to the provisions of the Platform Rules, the Bank shall assess the potential impact of those amendments on existing Funds and inform the Contributors thereof.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The amendments shall be deemed approved by the Contributors if they have not addressed a written objection to the Bank within 15 Business Days of dispatch of the notification by the Bank regarding the amendments.</P>
<P class="p632 ft110">If one or more Contributors object(s) to the amendments proposed, these Contributors are entitled to terminate the Contribution Agreement they entered into with the Bank with immediate effect within the timeframe set out above and to ask for the refund of the portion not invested into operations, if any, and subject to the deduction of any applicable fees, costs, losses, and charges, of their Contribution Paid if the amendments proposed by the Bank:</P>
<P class="p687 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft167">prevent such Contributor to continue to participate to the Platform in compliance with the laws and regulations applicable to it;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p642 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft103">impose on the Contributors to increase the amount of their Contributions; or</SPAN></P>

<P class="p565 ft5">A Contributor willing to terminate the Contribution Agreement pursuant to the termination process described above shall give evidence to the Bank and the other Contributors in the Fund that it is affected by an event listed under items <NOBR>(i)-(iii)</NOBR> above.</P>
<P class="p682 ft110">If an amendment to the provisions of the Platform Rules has a negative impact on one or more Funds, the relevant Contributors’ Committees shall decide whether to continue the affected Funds or to terminate them in accordance with Article 11.1 of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p639 ft5">Each Contributor acknowledges and agrees that technical amendments (such as, but not limited to, correction of drafting errors, numbering of Articles in the Platform Rules or crossor external references in the Platform Rules) and amendments that do not affect the substance of any provisions of these Platform Rules may be made unilaterally by the Bank. The Bank shall immediately inform the Contributors of those technical or minor amendments.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">13.2. Order of precedence</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">In the event of any inconsistency or conflict between the terms of the Platform Rules, a Contribution Agreement and those of the corresponding Fund Description, the following order of priority shall apply:</P>
<P class="p642 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">the Contribution Agreement (as between the Bank and the relevant Contributor);</SPAN></P>
<P class="p658 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">the Fund Description; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p690 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">the Platform Rules.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p691 ft5">In the event that there is more than one Contribution Agreement between the Bank and a Contributor in relation to the same Fund, then in the event of any inconsistency or conflict between the two, the later shall prevail as between the Bank and that Contributor.</P>
<P class="p692 ft125">14.</P>
<P class="p693 ft125">15. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 14</SPAN></P>
<P class="p694 ft122">SEVERABILITY</P>
<P class="p682 ft110">If, at any time, any of the provisions under these Platform Rules is or becomes illegal, invalid or unenforceable in any respect under the law of any jurisdiction, neither the legality, validity or enforceability of the remaining provisions of these Platform Rules nor of such provisions under the law of any other jurisdiction shall in any way be affected or impaired thereby.</P>

<P class="p696 ft125">16. <SPAN class="ft122">ARTICLE 15</SPAN></P>
<P class="p697 ft122">DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND GOVERNING LAW</P>
<P class="p495 ft31">15.1 Amicable resolution of disputes</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The parties having agreed to these Platform Rules shall endeavour to settle amicably any dispute or complaint relating to the interpretation, application or fulfilment of these Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31">15.2 Jurisdiction</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">For the purposes of any dispute arising in relation to these Platform Rules, the parties hereby submit to the jurisdiction of the Court of Justice of the European Union.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">15.3 Governing law</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">These Platform Rules are governed by, and shall be construed in accordance with, the laws of the <NOBR>Grand-Duchy</NOBR> of Luxembourg.</P>
