<P class="p699 ft122">ANNEX I</P>
<P class="p700 ft122">RECEIPT OF THIRD PARTY FINANCING</P>
<P class="p566 ft31">With a view to reinforcing complementarities and coordination with other parties’ activities that are in line with the objectives and guiding principles of the Platform, (other countries, International Financial Institutions, funds, foundations, private and banking entities etc.) the Contributors’ Committee of a Fund may authorize Third Party Financing in relation to that Fund.</P>
<P class="p656 ft168">Capitalised terms used in this Annex and not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning given to such terms in the Platform Rules to which this Annex is attached.</P>
<P class="p93 ft31">Article 1 Third Party Financing</P>
<P class="p565 ft5">Third Parties may contribute funds to a Fund under the Platform subject to the approval by the Bank and to the unanimous approval by the Contributors’ Committee of the relevant Fund. Once approved as eligible resources for the relevant Fund, Third Party Financing is subject to the special terms and conditions set forth in this Annex.</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">The approval of Third Party Financing does not result in the Third Party acquiring the status of Contributor and does not give the right to the Third Party concerned to be represented in the Contributors’ Committee of the relevant Fund and to participate in its meetings, written procedures or in any governance structure of the relevant Fund.</P>
<P class="p566 ft5">The Bank shall act as an intermediary with respect to Third Party Financing. In this respect, Third Party Financing shall not be recognized as Contributions in the Fund’s financial statements.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">Article 2 Third Party Agreement</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">Subject to the approval of the Bank’s Governing Bodies and the Contributors’ Committee of the relevant Fund, the Bank may sign, in its role of Administrator, an agreement with the relevant Third Party (the “Third Party Agreement”) specifying the name of the Third Party (including name of the contact person), nature of the Third Party Financing, applicable rules and its use. The use of the Third Party Financing shall be in line with the general purposes of the Platform and the related Fund, and for the operations approved as indicated in the Third Party Agreement.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">Article 3 Amount and Payment Modalities of Third Party Financing</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">The Third Party Agreement shall in principle include the total amount and payment modalities of the Third Party Financing. When such elements are not included in the Third Party Agreement at the time of the signature, the Contributors’ Committee of the relevant Fund shall be separately informed about the precise amount and payment modalities of the Third Party Financing under the Third Party Agreement, as soon as practically possible. Funds shall be committed exclusively in euros.</P>
<P class="p701 ft5">39</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p0 ft102">41</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_124">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p568 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p569 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p494 ft31">Article 4 Rules Applicable to Third Party Financing</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Proposals for potential operations funded from the Third Party Financing shall be submitted for approval to the Bank’s Governing Bodies and the Contributors’ Committee of the relevant Fund shall be informed about the approved operations.</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Third Party Financing shall be governed by the terms and conditions specified in the Third Party Agreement, including the use of such funds, reporting obligations, payment modalities, visibility, dispute settlement.</P>
<P class="p422 ft5">Article 12 of the Platform Rules shall apply with respect to Third Party Financing.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">Article 5 Bank Account for Third Party Financing</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Bank shall open a separate account in its accounting books for each Fund under which Third Party Financing has been approved. This account shall be called “Fund [<SPAN class="ft169"></SPAN>] – Financing from Third Party” for the receipt of the Third Party Financing, the disbursement of the monies and the Bank’s fees, and any potential remuneration as indicated in the Third Party Agreement.</P>
<P class="p422 ft5">Article 7 of the Platform Rules shall apply with respect to Third Party Financing.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">Article 6 Financial Reporting</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Bank shall provide financial reporting to substantiate the use of the Third Party Financing in accordance with the Article 9 of the Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p73 ft31">Article 7 Audit</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">Movements from the separate account opened for Third Party Financing may be subject to a separate external audit in accordance with the provisions of the Article 10 of the Platform Rules.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31">Article 8 General Reporting Obligations</P>
<P class="p571 ft5">The Bank shall ensure that the Contributors’ Committee of the relevant Fund is comprehensively informed on an annual basis with respect to all operations and activities financed from Third Party Financing.</P>

<P class="p703 ft122">ANNEX II</P>
<P class="p704 ft122">ASSET MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES</P>
<P class="p495 ft31">Preamble</P>
<P class="p577 ft5">The assets constituting the Platform Outstanding Balance from time to time which are under treasury management by the EIB (the “<SPAN class="ft31">Platform’s Assets</SPAN>”) shall be managed in accordance with the principles of sound financial management and following appropriate prudential rules in accordance with the principles laid down in Section I below. These assets shall be invested at the risk of the Contributors according to the guidelines as set out in Section II below. In this document, “Unitary Fund” means the pooled investment portfolio established by the EIB by the Deed Poll of 1 July 2009 as supplemented and amended from time to time and as defined in the corresponding Information Memorandum.</P>
<P class="p73 ft117">Section I - Principles Relating to the Platform Outstanding Balance</P>
<P class="p422 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">The EIB shall manage Platform’s Assets in accordance with the following principles:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p578 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">The risk exposure taken on the Platform’s Assets shall be limited to the capital invested and returns earned thereon.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p559 ft110"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft170">While executing transactions on behalf of the Platform, the EIB shall apply the same standards of due diligence and care it normally applies when managing its own treasury portfolios or its other mandates. While purchasing securities at any time, either on the primary market or the secondary market, the EIB shall guarantee equal treatment among the different portfolios under management. In this context, it shall not purchase securities of the same issue at the same time on more advantageous conditions for its own account or for the account of any other portfolio under management.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p593 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">Management of the assets shall be based on the best practice of the asset management industry and on the traditional prudential rules applied in financial activities. Management shall comply with the risk limitations set out under these Asset Management Guidelines. Particular care shall need to be taken to ensure that the managed assets provide sufficient liquidity in relation to the commitments to which the assets must respond, while still optimizing the return that is compatible with maintaining a </SPAN><NOBR>high-degree</NOBR> of security and stability over <NOBR>long-term.</NOBR></P>
<P class="p559 ft110"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft171">The EIB shall not be authorized to enter into speculative transactions or to borrow from the market to cover any liquidity gap. Unforeseen cash payments that are not sufficiently covered by cash holdings shall be covered adequately by the sale of assets. Reverse repo and collateralised securities lending transactions are authorised at the discretion of the EIB subject to the limitations set out in these Asset Management Guidelines.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p705 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(v)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">A performance index, taken as a benchmark shall be defined by the EIB and shall be in line with the existing benchmark used for other </SPAN><NOBR>third-party</NOBR> portfolios.</P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(vi)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft113">All investments need to respect the limits set out hereto.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p593 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(vii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft152">In accordance with the operational cash flow forecast, the EIB shall take the necessary measures to manage the placement of the Platform’s Assets in order to execute all payments in a timely manner.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p600 ft5">41</P>

<P class="p706 ft5"><SPAN class="ft28">(viii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft153">Securities transactions shall be based on the principle of “delivery versus payment”; delivery and payment to clearing systems are authorized.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p585 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(ix)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">The sale of assets is authorized, among others, if the securities no longer correspond to the criteria set out hereto or with a view to balancing the maturity profile or enhancing overall portfolio performance.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p422 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(x)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">The EIB shall regularly supervise the continuous respect of the limits set out hereto.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p631 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Funds’ Assets may be invested in EUR. Hedging instruments may be considered if relevant and </SPAN><NOBR>cost-efficient.</NOBR></P>
<P class="p73 ft117">Section II: Guidelines</P>
<P class="p620 ft5">The EIB shall manage the Funds’ Assets in accordance with the principles set out in Section I above.</P>
<P class="p495 ft155"><SPAN class="ft172">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft173">Portfolio structure</SPAN></P>
<P class="p573 ft5">The portfolio maturity structure shall reflect the projected cash flows from the Platform / Funds. Sufficient assets shall be placed in monetary assets to cover the short term (less than one year) outflows, at a proportion to be fixed in the annual investment strategy.</P>
<P class="p585 ft5"><SPAN class="ft172">1.1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft154">The remaining assets may be allocated to medium and long term instruments, with a maximum remaining maturity of 10 years and six months from the payment date (medium and </SPAN><NOBR>long-term</NOBR> portfolio).</P>
<P class="p588 ft5"><SPAN class="ft172">1.2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft154">Should the requirements of efficient portfolio management or some other grounded reasons require so and/or if the portfolio of asset management is smaller than EUR 100 million the EIB may allocate more or all of the assets in the units of the Unitary Fund. The EIB may in any case temporarily allocate more or all of the assets in the units of the Unitary Fund pending investment of the relevant part of the assets to the medium and long term instruments.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft155"><SPAN class="ft172">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft173">Types of investment</SPAN></P>
<P class="p610 ft110">The monetary assets may comprise units in the Unitary Fund, and other short term instruments with maturities up to 397 days at value date including fixed rate bonds (with such remaining maturity) and floating rate notes of up to 2 years of remaining maturity. It is understood that the Unitary Fund shall constitute the preferred investment option for the monetary assets in EUR. In case of unsecured bank deposits, the time to maturity should not exceed 95 days at value date. Considering the portion of the monetary assets invested in unsecured bank deposits, due consideration should be given to prevailing market conditions and risks. The remaining assets may include fixed rate bonds with remaining maturity longer than 397 days and floating rate bonds with more than 2 years of remaining maturity.</P>

<P class="p593 ft5"><SPAN class="ft177">3.1.1</SPAN><SPAN class="ft179">The EIB Unitary Fund operating and managed in accordance with the Deed Poll and its information memorandum, shall be eligible. <P class="p593 ft5"><SPAN class="ft177">3.1.2</SPAN><SPAN class="ft179">The banks authorised to receive term deposits shall be rated at least </SPAN><NOBR>P-1</NOBR> <NOBR>short-term</NOBR> Moody's or equivalent. Should the nominal size of the total portfolio exceed EUR 2 billion, increased maximum amounts of respectively EUR 125 million and EUR 60 million shall apply;</P>
<P class="p728 ft5"><SPAN class="ft186"></SPAN><SPAN class="ft187">the EIB and the Contributors may agree on further rating/maturity limits.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft5"><SPAN class="ft177">3.3</SPAN><SPAN class="ft178">Applicable Rating</SPAN></P>
<P class="p566 ft5">Securities should be rated at least by one of the rating agencies Standard and Poor's, Fitch or Moody's. In the absence of all bond/issue ratings, the respective issuer ratings (in case of guaranteed positions the guarantor ratings) shall be considered.</P>
<P class="p495 ft5">Loss of required rating</P>
<P class="p565 ft5">In case of a loss of required rating, the EIB shall endeavor to replace the relevant assets in the portfolio by other assets of adequate quality respecting the relevant limits. Alternatively, the EIB may analyze, among other factors, the remaining maturity of the asset and the probability of repayment at scheduled maturity, and as a result of this analysis decide to keep such assets.</P>
<P class="p583 ft5">Member State securities (including securities guaranteed by Member States) may be kept in an event of loss of required rating(s).</P>

<P class="p473 ft5"><SPAN class="ft177">3.4</SPAN><SPAN class="ft178">Concentration limits</SPAN></P>
<P class="p677 ft5"><SPAN class="ft177">3.4.1</SPAN><SPAN class="ft179">The total exposure to the same issuer or counterparty (consolidated at the TOP parent level) shall not exceed 10% (in the case of Member States, 20%) of the total amount of that portfolio.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p588 ft5"><SPAN class="ft177">3.4.2</SPAN><SPAN class="ft179">Should the total amount of assets in the portfolio be lower than EUR 100 million, the limit in 3.4.1. shall not apply. In this case however, a maximum exposure to any single issuer or counterparty should not exceed EUR 20 million.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p631 ft5"><SPAN class="ft177">3.4.3</SPAN><SPAN class="ft179">The total investment in an issue must not exceed 10% of the total nominal outstanding amount of the issue.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p495 ft155"><SPAN class="ft172">4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft173">Securities lending and repos</SPAN></P>
<P class="p573 ft5">The EIB is authorised, but is not under any obligation, to enter into reverse repo or collateralised securities lending operations with leading financial institutions complying with the criteria laid down for <NOBR>short-term</NOBR> investments under 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 above and with securities clearing companies.</P>

<P class="p731 ft117">Schedule 2 to the Contribution Agreement: Fund Description</P>
<P class="p732 ft31">ACP Trust Fund</P>
<P class="p733 ft31">Member State Compartment</P>
<P class="p734 ft5">The Fund is organized through the contractual establishment of an individual fund under the EIB’s <NOBR>multi-region,</NOBR> <NOBR>multi-contributor</NOBR> and <NOBR>multi-sector</NOBR> Partnerships Platform for Funds and is made pursuant to the Platform Rules. Capitalised terms used in this Fund Description and not otherwise defined herein shall be interpreted in accordance with the meaning given to such terms in the Platform Rules and in the applicable Contribution Agreement.</P>
<P class="p76 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft188">Background and purpose</SPAN></P>
<P class="p510 ft47"><SPAN class="ft5">The </SPAN><NOBR>EC-EIB</NOBR> Joint Understanding on the <NOBR>re-use</NOBR> of the ACP IF reflows <SPAN class="ft5">agreed on 3 December 2020 stated that reflows from the ACP Investment Facility would be transferred, once they become available, to the EU budget and implemented by the Bank under a </SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft5">single-package</SPAN></NOBR><SPAN class="ft5"> approach consisting of:</SPAN></P>
<P class="p735 ft5"><SPAN class="ft143">-</SPAN><SPAN class="ft189">An EFSD+ guarantee to the EIB for ACP private sector operations as a new dedicated investment window under EFSD+ with </SPAN><NOBR>intermediate-high</NOBR> risk funded by a share of the IF reflows (overall 50%);</P>
<P class="p736 ft5"><SPAN class="ft143">-</SPAN><SPAN class="ft189">A contribution in the form of grants to a trust fund to support the highest risk private sector operations in ACP countries funded by the remainder of the ACP IF reflows. Although held and managed by EIB, it would be considered a de facto new dedicated investment window under EFSD+ (ACP Trust Fund – EC Compartment);</SPAN></P>
<P class="p737 ft5"><SPAN class="ft143">-</SPAN><SPAN class="ft189">the provision of a replacement guarantee to the EIB under EFSD+ in respect of the ACP Infrastructure Package.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p738 ft110">Council Decision (EU) 2020/2233 of 23 December 2020 concerning the commitment of the funds stemming from reflows under the ACP Investment Facility from operations under the 9th, 10th and 11th European Development Funds approved the transfer of the ACP IF reflows after 30 June 2021 as contributions to NDICI <NOBR>–Global</NOBR> Europe /EFSD+ as external assigned revenue. The Council Decision also mentioned the earmarking of the ACP IF reflows for ACP countries, the EIB’s role as the implementing entity for ensuring the transferred reflows support ACP countries, and the concept of supporting ACP countries under a <NOBR>single-package</NOBR> approach without business interruption.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">The ACP Trust Fund is an umbrella structure and consists of, initially, two separate compartments:</P>
<P class="p739 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">ACP Trust Fund – EC Compartment funded by ACP Investment Facility Reflows (50% of all reflows paid in by the EIB to the EU); and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p740 ft136"><SPAN class="ft28">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft190">the Fund, also known as the Member States compartment of the ACP Trust Fund, sourced by funds of interested EU Member States from previous ACP mandates deposited in accounts at the EIB, and/or other Member State contributions.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p741 ft5">Additional compartments may be added at a later stage, subject to the approval of the Contributors’ Committee, with a view to collecting other contributors/donors’ contributions, if deemed appropriate/necessary.</P>
<P class="p742 ft110">The ACP Trust Fund – EC Compartment will focus on private sector operations characterized by high risk, expected to achieve high impact, such as equity, quasi equity, local currency lending, lending to fragile countries and <NOBR>co-financing</NOBR> with EFSD Guarantees. It may also be deployed in ancillary Technical Assistance and to meet the requirements in terms of risk sharing <NOBR>(“skin-in-the-game”)</NOBR> for the ACP EFSD+ Guarantee</P>

</DIV>
</DIV>

<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p492 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p493 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p744 ft5">(fourth dedicated EIB window under NDICI – Global Europe) and/or eventually for the EFSD+ Open access for ACP countries.</P>
<P class="p745 ft5">The Fund will be deployed only in the form of grants for technical assistance, investment grants, interest rate subsidies and hedging solutions for local currencies<SPAN class="ft41">1</SPAN>.</P>
<P class="p746 ft31">2. Objectives of the Fund</P>
<P class="p747 ft110">The Fund will support ACP partner countries’ efforts to achieve the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030, fostering sustainable economic, social and environmental development of ACP countries, with the primary aim of eradicating poverty, in line with <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe key guiding principles in the implementation of the EFSD+ (Art. 31 of the Regulation) and the EFSD+ Strategic Orientations. Investments proposed in Africa should also be in line with the Global Gateway <NOBR>Africa-Europe</NOBR> Investment Package.</P>
<P class="p522 ft5">The main objectives of the Fund shall be:</P>
<P class="p748 ft5">- policy first approach fully aligned with the <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe programming documents and the Team Europe Initiatives;</P>
<P class="p749 ft5">- promoting inclusive, <NOBR>gender-responsive</NOBR> and sustainable economic growth and development especially in least developed countries and fragile countries, with the ultimate objective of reducing poverty, contributing to achieving the SDGs and creating sustainable jobs;</P>
<P class="p748 ft5">- fight against climate change and for environmental protection and to ensure alignment with the objectives of the Paris Climate Agreement;</P>
<P class="p749 ft5">- measurable development impact, additionality, <NOBR>co-financing</NOBR> and no <NOBR>crowding-out,</NOBR> demonstration effect and adherence to social, environmental and fiscal standards; and</P>
<P class="p748 ft5">- addressing market failures and suboptimal investment situations, delivering innovative products and mobilizing private sector funds.</P>
<P class="p750 ft27"><SPAN class="ft130">1 </SPAN>Subject to the conditions set out in Article 6 (<SPAN class="ft48">Permitted instruments</SPAN>).</P>
<P class="p751 ft5">48</P>

<P class="p0 ft102">50</P>

</DIV>

<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p504 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p505 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p752 ft5">Under the Investment Facility established under the Cotonou Agreement, the EIB managed a subsidies envelope<SPAN class="ft41">2 </SPAN>to support the preparation and implementation of the projects it financed in the ACP region, providing grants in the form of interest rate subsidies and technical assistance to its borrowers and final beneficiaries.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">The mobilization under the Fund of Member State funds from legacy mandates would make up for the absence of a dedicated subsidy envelope under the <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe mandate. It would allow the EIB to continue providing concessional lending, in line with global debt sustainability frameworks, as well as crucial technical assistance to get new projects off the ground and assist promoters in their implementation, especially in least developed countries and fragile countries.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">The objective of the Fund is to mobilise Member State resources, in the form of grants for technical assistance, interest rate subsidies, investment grants and hedging solutions for local currency<SPAN class="ft41">3</SPAN>, for operations in ACP countries either under the ACP Trust Fund – EC Compartment or under the EFSD+ EIB dedicated windows for sovereign lending (IW1) in ACP countries and ACP private sector lending (IW4), benefiting from the EU guarantee, to enhancing the transformative effect and the development impact of the EIB operations in the ACP region, by:</P>
<P class="p753 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">-</SPAN><SPAN class="ft189">providing concessional financing to facilitate investment in vital infrastructure. The overall financing cost for the beneficiaries will be lower as a result of the grants and therefore the financial viability of investments will be increased with significant economic returns that promote an enabling environment for inclusive growth and job creation;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p735 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">-</SPAN><SPAN class="ft189">supporting higher risk or lower financial return investments that can potentially achieve enhanced social and economic impact and/or reach underserved or vulnerable groups (e.g. women and youth);</SPAN></P>
<P class="p754 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">-</SPAN><SPAN class="ft189">supporting promoters to prepare and successfully implement projects and to build local capacity; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p755 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">-</SPAN><SPAN class="ft189">supporting the deployment of local currency lending</SPAN><SPAN class="ft41">4</SPAN>.</P>
<P class="p756 ft5">The Fund also aims to contribute to the <NOBR>cross-cutting</NOBR> general objectives and targets established under <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe including on social inclusion and human development, gender equality, climate action and biodiversity.</P>
<P class="p138 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft188">Eligible Activities</SPAN></P>
<P class="p757 ft5">Operations shall be eligible for support under the Fund if (i) they would be eligible under <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe; (ii) they are eligible pursuant to the EIB’s financing policies; and (iii) they are compatible with the criteria listed below.</P>
<P class="p758 ft155">General</P>
<P class="p759 ft127">Pursuant to the Platform Rules, the Fund shall operate in full accordance with the EIB’s policies and guidelines, including in relation to environmental, social and gender policies, as well as those related to <NOBR>anti-fraud,</NOBR> fight against tax evasion, tax avoidance, harmful tax practices, <NOBR>anti-money</NOBR> laundering and fight against financing of terrorism, market</P>
<P class="p760 ft27"><SPAN class="ft42">2</SPAN><SPAN class="ft141">EUR 634m for </SPAN><NOBR>2014-2020,</NOBR> according to 11th European Development Fund Internal Agreement, OJ L</P>
<P class="p761 ft129">210, 6.8.2013 p.1</P>
<P class="p0 ft129"><SPAN class="ft42">3</SPAN><SPAN class="ft191">Subject to the conditions set out in Article 6 (</SPAN><SPAN class="ft192">Permitted instruments</SPAN>)</P>
<P class="p0 ft27"><SPAN class="ft130">4 </SPAN>Subject to the conditions set out in Article 6 (<SPAN class="ft48">Permitted instruments</SPAN>)</P>
<P class="p762 ft5">49</P>
</DIV>

<P class="p0 ft102">51</P>

<DIV id="page_134">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p492 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p493 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p763 ft5">abuse, <NOBR>non-cooperation</NOBR> with <NOBR>non-transparent</NOBR> and uncooperative jurisdictions, procurement, complaints mechanism and transparency policies.</P>
<P class="p764 ft5">Funding received shall be used according to the general <NOBR>cross-cutting</NOBR> principles applicable to the EIB’s activities, including the following:</P>
<P class="p765 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Protection of human rights and safeguarding against social, climate and environmental risks that should be achieved by ensuring compliance with the EIB’s environmental and social standards, as well as the EIB’s Climate Action Statement;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p766 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Protection of women’s rights that should be achieved through the application of the EIB’s social standards, and the promotion of gender equality and women’s economic empowerment (GEWE) based on the implementation of the EIB Group Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment Strategy;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p765 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Conflict sensitivity approach that should be achieved through avoiding investments being impacted by, or indeed triggering, conflict, social tensions and violence through the application of a conflict sensitivity approach to operations in fragile or </SPAN><NOBR>conflict-affected</NOBR> contexts as appropriate;</P>
<P class="p766 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Ownership that should be ensured through consultations with the beneficiary countries and ensuring the alignment and complementarity of operations with relevant regional, national and local strategies and priorities;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p524 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(e)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft107">Cost-Sharing</SPAN></NOBR> that should be achieved through ensuring that, whenever possible, final beneficiaries shall make an appropriate contribution to the operations financed under the Fund;</P>
<P class="p524 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(f)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft109">Cost-Efficiency</SPAN></NOBR> that should be achieved by ensuring that only a justifiable proportion of grants/subsidies shall be provided alongside other sources of financing. It shall be ensured that the costs of implementation of the operations shall always be reasonable;</P>
<P class="p766 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(g)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Sustainability that should be achieved by seeking to ensure an improved local capacity by transferring knowledge to final beneficiaries and maintaining the impact of the investment also beyond the life of the operation;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p524 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(h)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Catalytic Impact that should be achieved by ensuring that resources are provided only for activities that can contribute to the subsequent mobilisation of additional funds, partners, or further assistance in supported areas; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p524 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Promotion of open market that should be achieved by ensuring that overcompensation is avoided and that supported operations do not distort the functioning of the market.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p767 ft5">When proposing Operations to the Fund, the Bank shall take into account the OECD DAC Blended Finance Principles and also the development effectiveness principles defined by the Global Partnership for Effective Development Cooperation.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">4.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft146">Investment Priorities</SPAN></P>
<P class="p768 ft5">Lawful activities in all economic sectors are eligible for financial support under the Fund with the exclusion of activities with negative social or environmental impact. Sector coverage shall duly take into consideration the relevant EU regional and country strategies.</P>
<P class="p769 ft127">It should be noted though that the following section provides a broad outline of the Fund’s operational focus and should neither be considered to represent an exhaustive list of</P>
<P class="p770 ft5">50</P>
</DIV>

<P class="p0 ft102">52</P>
</DIV>

<DIV id="page_135">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p504 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p505 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p771 ft5">areas, sectors or activities covered under the Fund and nor should be interpreted as firm investment commitments.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">In line with the provisions of the <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe, priority should be given to operations which have a high impact on job creation. According to the EFSD+ Strategic Orientations, the EU programming process has identified the following overarching priorities:</P>
<P class="p772 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft109">Sub-Saharan</SPAN></NOBR> Africa: Green transition and fight against climate change; Access to Finance; Human Capital; Sustainable Cities and Digitalisation;</P>
<P class="p773 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Caribbean: Green Deal; Economic Resilience and Trade and Governance; Security and Human Development; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p774 ft110"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft193">Pacific: Climate Action and Environmental Sustainability; Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Development; Fundamental Values, Human Development, Peace and Security. The projects should contribute to the Team Europe Initiatives </SPAN><NOBR>“Green-Blue</NOBR> alliance” for the Pacific, “Forestry, Climate Change and Biodiversity Nexus” for Papua New Guinea and “A new Green Deal” for Timor Leste.</P>
<P class="p775 ft5">The overarching objectives of the Fund are in line with the strategic orientations approved by the EFSD+ Strategic Board:</P>
<P class="p758 ft5"><SPAN class="ft28">1.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft108">Green Deal</SPAN></P>
<P class="p776 ft5"><SPAN class="ft28">2.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft108">Global Gateway</SPAN></P>
<P class="p758 ft5"><SPAN class="ft28">3.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft108">Jobs and Inclusive Growth</SPAN></P>
<P class="p93 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">5.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft188">Geographic scope</SPAN></P>
<P class="p510 ft5">Projects eligible for financing under the Fund shall be carried out in one or more countries that are considered eligible countries under the ACP Trust Fund – EC Compartment (<SPAN class="ft31">“Eligible Countries”</SPAN>) and/or for the benefit of one or more Eligible Countries, regardless of the domicile of the EIB contractual counterparties, provided that EU horizontal provisions in accordance with the <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe Regulation are met (e.g. AML, NCJ). The list of Eligible Countries is set out in Appendix A to this Fund Description.</P>
<P class="p777 ft5">An increasing volume of transactions will be carried out in least developed countries and fragile countries in the region, subject to the demand of the market and guidance from the <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe programming documents and the policy first approach.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">6.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft188">Permitted instruments and policy guidelines</SPAN></P>
<P class="p778 ft5">Contributions may only be made in euro, but operations may be denominated in euro or in United States dollars.</P>
<P class="p776 ft31">6.1 Permitted instruments</P>
<P class="p758 ft5">The resources of the Fund may be deployed in the form of:</P>
<P class="p779 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Technical Assistance and Advisory Services (TA&AS): an instrument aimed at supporting preparation and implementation of investments through institutional capacity building and the financing of e.g. </SPAN><NOBR>pre-feasibility</NOBR> and feasibility studies, design and tender documents, institutional and legal appraisals, environmental and social impact assessments, project management, as well as financing upstream studies, gender analysis or advisory services to beneficiaries.</P>
<P class="p762 ft5">51</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p0 ft102">53</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_136">
<DIV id="p136dimg1">
<INGENBILD zsrc="HB0399136x1.jpg/" id="p136img1">
</DIV>


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p492 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p493 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p780 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Investment grants: </SPAN><NOBR>non-reimbursable</NOBR> contribution to finance tangible or intangible components of a project or venture, in joint or parallel <NOBR>co-financing</NOBR> with other investors. In particular, the investment grants may decrease the investment costs for the beneficiary through financing part of the investment or through an increase of the concessionality of the financing package of a given project. They may also target specific project components which have substantial demonstrable social or environmental benefits or which can mitigate negative environmental or social impacts.</P>
<P class="p781 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft108">Interest rate subsidies: the provision of a grant amount to an investor financing an operation to enable it to make </SPAN><NOBR>long-term</NOBR> finance available in flexible ways that reduce the total amount of debt service to be paid by the borrower. Such subsidies can therefore be applied upfront or over time, and shall be granted so as to avoid market distortions. Financing operations benefiting from interest rate subsidies shall be in line with the minimum concessionality requirements<SPAN class="ft41">5 </SPAN>in accordance with the Joint World <NOBR>Bank-IMF</NOBR> Debt Sustainability Framework for Low Income Countries.</P>
<P class="p782 ft110"><SPAN class="ft5">d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft157">Hedging solutions for local currency: the provision of grants for the </SPAN><NOBR>set-up</NOBR> of a facility which would support lending in local currency for the Bank and potentially as well for the other European DFIs. This is a permitted instrument for the Fund but will only be deployed upon a future decision of the Management Committee of the Bank to implement the instrument under the Fund following the establishment of appropriate procedures and controls by the services of the Bank.</P>
<P class="p658 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">6.2</SPAN><SPAN class="ft194">Policy guidelines on interest rate subisidies</SPAN></P>
<P class="p522 ft5">The policy guidelines on interest rate subsidies shall be as follows:</P>
<P class="p523 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Interest rate subsidies may be capitalised or may be used in the form of grants paid up front.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p781 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">For infrastructure projects in the least developed countries, in </SPAN><NOBR>post-conflict</NOBR> countries and in <NOBR>post-natural</NOBR> disaster countries, considered a prerequisite for private sector development, the interest rate of the loan will be reduced, as necessary in order to achieve at least the minimum concessionality in line with IMF requirements (typically expected to be 35% or above). In this case, the subsidies are essentially justified by macroeconomic considerations, notably the need to limit public indebtedness. Nevertheless, this raises the issue of avoiding that they distort the market which is best achieved by structuring the operation in two stages, whereby the subsidised loan is made to the State for <NOBR>on-lending</NOBR> on <NOBR>market-related</NOBR> terms to the public promoter. However, it can only be used if the State is an adequate counterpart and if other, <NOBR>project-specific</NOBR> considerations, allow.</P>
<P class="p783 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft108">For projects which involve restructuring operations in the framework of privatisation or for projects with substantial and clearly demonstrable social or environmental benefits. In such cases, loans may be extended with an interest rate subsidy, the amount and form of which will be decided with respect to the particular characteristics of the project. However, the interest rate subsidy shall not be higher than required by a respective IMF programme and the level of</SPAN></P>
<P class="p784 ft196"><SPAN class="ft158">5</SPAN><SPAN class="ft195">In accordance with the IMF Debt Limits Policy (DLP) and the World Bank’s Sustainable Development Finance Policy (SDFP), restrictive borrowing conditions apply to countries with high levels of debt and poverty, IDA eligible countries. Those countries should receive financing on concessional terms, so as to ease the burden of future debt service on budgets and external positions. A loan is concessional when it contains a grant element of at least 35 per cent.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p785 ft5">52</P>
</DIV>
<DIV id="id_2">
<P class="p0 ft102">54</P>
</DIV>
</DIV>
<DIV id="page_137">


<DIV id="id_1">
<P class="p786 ft100">Prop. 2023/24:99 Bilaga 3</P>
<P class="p787 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p788 ft5">subsidy will not exceed the cost of such restructuring operations or the cost of the environmental and social components, unless justified by other development objectives and specifically decided.</P>
<P class="p508 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">The subsidy will be applied with the utmost transparency: the reasons underlying the need for concessional funding, and, when applicable, the level of concessionality recommended, will all be clearly identified.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p511 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">e)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">In case of early repayment of a loan by the promoter, and depending on the purpose for which it was earmarked, the subsidy may be recovered on a </SPAN><NOBR>pro-rata</NOBR> basis.</P>
<P class="p76 ft31"><SPAN class="ft134">6.3</SPAN><SPAN class="ft194">Policy guidelines on Technical Assistance and Advisory Services</SPAN></P>
<P class="p344 ft5">The policy guidelines on Technical Assistance and Advisory Services (TA&AS) shall be as follows:</P>
<P class="p511 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">TA&AS can support either upstream activities such as policy and regulatory framework development, market and sector development as well as, within the project cycle, project identification and preparation, or downstream activities during project implementation, as further specified in the following paragraphs b) and c).</SPAN></P>
<P class="p789 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Upstream project preparation TA & AS aim at improving the overall business climate and contribute towards the identification and preparation of bankable projects. The expert services may include </SPAN><NOBR>inter-alia,</NOBR> market and sectorial masterplan studies, <NOBR>pre-feasibility</NOBR> and feasibility studies, preparation of tender documents, institutional and legal appraisals, environmental and social impact assessments and capacity building to governments, national entities, potential borrowers and final beneficiaries in order to improve local knowledge and skills.</P>
<P class="p508 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">Downstream project implementation TA & AS aim at enhancing overall project quality and sustainability through the provision of expert advisory services to private sector companies in project and business management that contribute also towards the institutional capacity building of local borrowers and final beneficiaries. Project quality is also raised in terms of environmental, social and governance standards as well as through regular audit requirements, ensuring that the project remains sustainable over the long run. To the extent possible TA & AS are deployed to ensure </SPAN><NOBR>know-how</NOBR> transfer and knowledge sharing.</P>
<P class="p789 ft110"><SPAN class="ft27">d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft157">The TA & AS instrument is generally seen as complementary to (EIB Global’s) funding activities in priority areas such as private sector support (intermediated </SPAN><NOBR>long-term</NOBR> loans to SMEs, risk capital instruments, microfinance, equity participation), environmental sustainability (water and wastewater projects, sector strategies, project management units, regulatory framework, environmental and social studies), regional integration and mobility (road construction, modernisation of railways and sea ports, regional transport schemes, regulatory framework, private participation in infrastructure, etc.), energy (increase of energy efficiency, promotion of renewable energy, provision of risk sharing instruments such as guarantee and insurance products to the private sector, etc.) and education and health (investment in infrastructure, improving quality and efficiency for health and education services deployment, <NOBR>private-public</NOBR> partnerships, project management units, training, etc.).</P>
<P class="p790 ft5">53</P>
</DIV>

<P class="p494 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">7.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft146">Eligible Counterparties</SPAN></P>
<P class="p521 ft5">Eligible counterparties under the Fund comprise:</P>
<P class="p791 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">private enterprises including large enterprises, project finance vehicles, SMEs and micro enterprises;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p523 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">intermediaries including commercial banks, financial institutions, and private equity funds;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p522 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">international organizations, multinational development banks;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p521 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(d)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">regional and national development banks; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p522 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(e)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">sovereigns, </SPAN><NOBR>sub-sovereigns</NOBR> and public corporations.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">8.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft188">Approval of operations</SPAN></P>
<P class="p521 ft5">The Fund will be subject to EFSD+ governance to ensure coherence.</P>
<P class="p745 ft5">The operation approval process will be built on the <NOBR>NDICI-Global</NOBR> Europe/EIB governance process applicable to other <NOBR>EIB-dedicated</NOBR> investment windows, as described below. Each operation will be subject to:</P>
<P class="p765 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">enhanced upstream coordination with pipeline sharing and pipeline review meetings between the Bank and the European Commission to assess the conformity of projects with the relevant country cooperation strategy or regional cooperation strategy or EU external policies;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p524 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(b)</SPAN><NOBR><SPAN class="ft114">Pre-appraisal</SPAN></NOBR> consultation: prior to the completion of the appraisal stage of a project, EIB shall request the opinion of the European Commission on the conformity of the project with the relevant EU policies, and in particular with the country or regional cooperation strategy concerned; and</P>
<P class="p524 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Eligibility assessment: the Bank will complete the eligibility fiche based on the outcome of its due diligence on the operation and the European Commission will have 15 business days to confirm whether that operation may become an operation under the ACP Trust Fund.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p745 ft5">Notwithstanding the provisions of Articles 6.3 and 6.4 of the Platform Rules, for any operation financed from the Fund, following the agreement of the European Commission, the Contributors' Committee shall be responsible for approving the allocation of funds in accordance with Article 5.8 of the Platform Rules. Where relevant, the Contributors’ Committee shall be provided with an extract of the information pertaining to the proposed operation contained in the eligibility fiche.</P>
<P class="p747 ft5">The decision making process of the Contributors’ Committee for the approval of the allocation of funds shall be carried out in accordance with the tacit procedure described in Article 5.8(b) of the Platform Rules, save that a <NOBR>10-business</NOBR> day deadline shall apply to any decision to be made thereunder. Decisions of the Contributors’ Committee in relation to the approval of the allocation of funds will be sought during a meeting (including virtual meetings), in accordance with Article 5.8(a) of the Platform Rules, in exceptional cases such as where the tacit procedure described in the previous sentence does not lead to the adoption of a favourable decision.</P>
<P class="p745 ft5">The decision from the Contributors’ Committee shall be sought before the relevant, if applicable, EIB Board of Directors’ approval in relation to the operation. For the avoidance of doubt, EIB Board of Directors’ approval may be obtained under rules of delegation established by the EIB governing bodies.</P>
<P class="p770 ft5">54</P>

<P class="p505 ft101">Corporate Use</P>
<P class="p752 ft5">In relation to the decision making process in accordance to the tacit procedure, only one representative of each Contributor, either the member or the alternate<SPAN class="ft41">6</SPAN>, as the case may be, is authorized to communicate to the Bank the approvals and/or objections of such Contributor in relation to operations and other issues on which the approval may be sought.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">Business day within the meaning of this Contribution Agreement means a day (other than a Saturday or Sunday) on which: (i) banks are open for general business in Luxembourg and Brussels; (ii) EIB is open for business in Luxembourg; and (iii) the Commission is open for business in Brussels.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">9.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft188">Fees</SPAN></P>
<P class="p510 ft5">Fees shall be charged in accordance with Article 7 of the Platform Rules in the currency, or one or more of the currencies, of the Fund Outstanding Balance at the time of payment of the fees.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">10.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft197">Accounting and reporting</SPAN></P>
<P class="p756 ft5">The financial reporting provisions of the Platform Rules in Article 9 shall apply<SPAN class="ft41">7</SPAN>. Accordingly, the account movements of the Fund will be incorporated into the consolidated statement of account movements of the Funds under the Platform.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">However, by derogation from Article 5.4(vii) of the Platform Rules, the financial statements of the Fund shall not be submitted to the Contributors’ Committee for approval. In accordance with Article 9.2 of the Platform Rules, the financial statements of the Fund shall be approved in line with financial statement approval procedures generally applied by EIB to third party mandates.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">In accordance with Article 9.4 (i) of the Platform Rules, the Bank will deliver to the Contributors Committee an annual operations progress report for information. By derogation from Article 9.4 (ii) and (iii) of the Platform Rules, the Bank will not deliver to the Contributors Committee <NOBR>bi-annual</NOBR> operation progress updates and operation completion reports.</P>
<P class="p595 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">11.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft197">Indicative Results Framework</SPAN></P>
<P class="p510 ft5">For measurable results, a results framework for the activities financed by the Fund shall be prepared by the Bank, once the Fund has started to support operations. The results framework shall be aligned, to the extent possible with the EFSD+ results measurement framework.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">The format, contents and frequency of the results framework shall be determined by the Bank and may be revised from time to time. It shall be used for reporting and evaluation purposes only. The current framework is the Additionality and Impact Measurement (AIM) framework<SPAN class="ft41">8</SPAN>.</P>
<P class="p595 ft27"><SPAN class="ft42">6</SPAN><SPAN class="ft198">In case of the alternate, acting under a specific delegation from the member.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p792 ft129"><SPAN class="ft42">7</SPAN><SPAN class="ft199">Contributors should note that this implies, according to Article 9.2 of the Platform Rules, that the Platform financial statements (all funds combined and incorporating statements of each Fund) will be shared with all contributors to all Platform funds, including entities that are not Contributors to the Fund.</SPAN></P>
<P class="p793 ft28"><SPAN class="ft42">8</SPAN><SPAN class="ft200">Additional information on AIM is available at: </SPAN><SPAN class="ft201">https://www.eib.org/en/projects/cycle/monitoring/aim.htm</SPAN></P>
<P class="p794 ft5">55</P>

<P class="p744 ft5">The results framework will include indicators reflecting, to the extent possible, the <SPAN class="ft47">exante </SPAN>expected sustainability of the projects, drawing on information collected during project preparation. The results indicators contained in the framework will be followed up after project completion, giving insights into sustainability <SPAN class="ft47">ex post</SPAN>.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">12.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft197">Evaluation</SPAN></P>
<P class="p795 ft110">The Bank may perform an evaluation of the operations carried out under the Fund. Such evaluation will aim at increasing transparency regarding the performance of the Fund and the operations funded thereunder, as well as at sharing and promoting lessons learnt. The evaluation shall be shared with the Contributors’ Committee, if performed.</P>
<P class="p233 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">13.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft149">Resources</SPAN></P>
<P class="p796 ft5">The Contributor wishes to contribute to the Fund the portion specified in the Contribution Agreement in relation to the amounts, present and future, held by the Bank for the account of the Contributor in respect of risk capital operations under the Yaoundé and Lomé conventions during the Contribution Period. Specifically:</P>
<P class="p524 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Special Accounts: Yaoundé I – Lomé 4b conventions mandated the EIB to manage loans and risk capital operations financed with resources from Member States</SPAN><SPAN class="ft41">9 </SPAN>(EDF). Special Accounts are opened in EIB’s books to record these transactions and Member States receive a report twice per year. A total amount of approximately EUR 131.4 million (excluding UK) has accumulated in these accounts at June 2023 and around EUR 78.7 million (excluding UK) are still expected in reflows during the Contribution Period of the Contribution Agreement; and</P>
<P class="p781 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">Lomé 4 bis Additional Resources (bridging facility – </SPAN><NOBR>ACP-EC</NOBR> Council Decision 2/2000 and 3/2002): In 2001, resources from unallocated amounts of the 6th, 7th and 8th EDFs were made available to the EIB for risk capital operations to support private sector development in ACP countries during the interim period before the entry into force of the Investment Facility. A total amount of approximately EUR 201.8 million (excluding UK) has accumulated in these accounts at June 2023 and EUR 7.5 million (excluding UK) are still expected in reflows during the Contribution Period of the Contribution Agreement.<SPAN class="ft41">10</SPAN></P>

<P class="p494 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">14.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft197">Foreign exchange risk and treasury management</SPAN></P>
<P class="p510 ft5">In order to manage operations that are not denominated in EUR, any part of the Fund Outstanding Balance may be converted from EUR to USD and <SPAN class="ft47">vice versa </SPAN>in accordance with the normal practice of the Bank. The foreign exchange risk arising from any conversion shall be borne by the Fund.</P>
<P class="p776 ft5">By derogation from Article 8.1 of the Platform Rules, the Bank shall:</P>
<P class="p799 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft107">as regards amounts of the Fund Outstanding Balance denominated in EUR invest such amounts only in the Unitary Fund of the Bank and not in accordance with the Asset Management Guidelines; and</SPAN></P>
<P class="p740 ft110"><SPAN class="ft27">(b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft203">as regards amounts of the Fund Outstanding Balance denominated in USD, keep such amounts on an account in the books of the Bank denominated in USD. The Bank shall apply to the daily balance of the account in USD an interest rate, without any floor or ceiling, that is equal to 3M </SPAN><NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term flat (the forwardlooking term Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) administered by CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) for a period of three (3) months) as of 06:00 a.m., New York City time, on the day that is two (2) U.S. Government Securities Business Days (being any day except for a Saturday, Sunday or a day on which The Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (or a successor) recommends that the fixed income departments of its members be closed for the entire day for the purpose of trading in U.S. government securities) prior to the start of each calculation period of three (3) months (save that the first and last calculation periods may be shorter) (the “<SPAN class="ft115">USD Interest Rate</SPAN>”). With respect to a calculation period, the Bank shall multiply the daily balance of such <NOBR>sub-account</NOBR> in USD by the USD Interest Rate for each day in that period and divide the result by 360. The amount of interest (the “<SPAN class="ft115">USD Interest Amount</SPAN>”) with respect to a calculation period shall be equal to the sum of the amounts of interest so determined and calculated by the Bank for each day in that period. If the USD Interest Amount for a calculation period is a positive number, the resources of the relevant account shall be increased by the USD Interest Amount. If the USD Interest Amount for a calculation period is a negative number, the resources of the relevant account shall be decreased by the absolute value of the USD Interest Amount.</P>
<P class="p800 ft5">If 3M <NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term in respect of the day for which it is required is not published by CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) or an authorized distributor and is not otherwise provided by CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) and the Bank has determined that a temporary discontinuation has occurred, the applicable rate for that day will be the last provided or published level of 3M USD- SOFR CME Term as at the day on which 3M <NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term was originally required.</P>
<P class="p801 ft5">If, as solely determined by the Bank, in respect of a day for which it is required 3M <NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term has been permanently discontinued but, in respect of that date CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) provides the <NOBR>forward-looking</NOBR> term SOFR for maturity periods that are, respectively, longer than and shorter than three (3) months, then the interpolated rate shall be used to determine the rate for that date.</P>

<P class="p494 ft5">If, as solely determined by the Bank,</P>
<P class="p519 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(i)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft109">in respect of the day for which it is required 3M </SPAN><NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term has been permanently discontinued and, in respect of that date the use of interpolated rate does not apply because there is either no shorter or no longer maturity;</P>
<P class="p804 ft5"><SPAN class="ft28">(ii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft151">a public statement or publication of information by on behalf of CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) of 3M </SPAN><NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term announces that it has ceased or will cease to provide 3M <NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term permanently or indefinitely, provided that, at the time of the statement or publication, there is no successor administrator or provider, as applicable, that will continue to provide 3M <NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term;</P>
<P class="p805 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(iii)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">a public statement or publication of information by the regulatory supervisor for CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator), the central bank for the currency of 3M </SPAN><NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term, an insolvency official with jurisdiction over CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator), a resolution authority with jurisdiction over CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) or a court or an entity with similar insolvency or resolution authority over CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) states that the CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) has ceased or will cease to provide the 3M <NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term permanently or indefinitely, provided that, at the time of the statement or publication, there is no successor administrator or provider that will continue to provide the 3M <NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term; or</P>
<P class="p806 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(iv)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft116">an event or a circumstance occurs which has the effect that the Bank is not or will not be permitted to use the </SPAN><NOBR>forward-looking</NOBR> term SOFR;</P>
<P class="p807 ft110">the rate for a day it is required occurring on or after any of the events described above with respect to 3M <NOBR>USD-SOFR</NOBR> CME Term will be the CME Term SOFR Recommended Rate for a period of three (3) months (meaning the rate, inclusive of any spread adjustments, recommended as the replacement for the forwardlooking term SOFR by CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) or, if CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) does not make a recommendation, a committee officially endorsed or convened by the Federal Reserve Board or the Federal Reserve Bank of New York or the supervisor of CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) for the purpose of recommending a replacement for the <NOBR>forward-looking</NOBR> term SOFR (which rate may be produced by another administrator) and as provided by CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited (or any successor administrator) or, if that rate is not provided by such administrator, published by an authorized distributor.</P>
<P class="p808 ft5">If CME Term SOFR Recommended Rate is not published in respect of a day for which it is required, or its use is no longer in accordance with the policies and practices of the Bank, the Bank may, after having consulted the Contributors, replace it with another benchmark rate and any appropriate adjustment to the spread, <NOBR>day-count</NOBR> fraction and/or calculation period, which it will determine in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.</P>

<P class="p494 ft31"><SPAN class="ft31">15.</SPAN><SPAN class="ft197">Amendments to Fund Description</SPAN></P>
<P class="p742 ft110">This Fund Description may be amended from time to time, subject to approval of the Bank and the approval of the Contributors’ Committee given by Contributors representing</P>
<P class="p810 ft5">(i) at least two thirds of the total amount of the Contributions received by the Bank since inception of the Fund and (ii) <NOBR>one-half</NOBR> plus one of the total number of Contributors to the Fund, or a majority of the total number of Contributors to the Fund if that is an odd number.</P>
<P class="p510 ft5">The Bank may at its own discretion amend the provisions of this Fund Description, to the extent such amendments result from a change in the Bank’s rules and policies or from the regulations applicable to the Bank’s activities or from the decisions of the Bank’s Governing Bodies (<SPAN class="ft31">“obligatory amendments”</SPAN>). If one or more Contributors object(s) to the introduction of obligatory amendments, those Contributors are entitled to terminate the Contribution Agreement they entered into with the Bank in relation to the Fund with immediate effect and to require the refund of the portion not committed to or invested in operations, and subject to the deduction of any applicable fees, costs, losses, and charges, of their Contribution Paid, if the obligatory amendments:</P>
<P class="p811 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(a)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft107">prevent such Contributor(s) continuing to participate in the Fund in compliance with the laws and regulations applicable to it;</SPAN></P>
<P class="p521 ft5"><SPAN class="ft5">(b)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft107">require such Contributor(s) to increase the amount of their Contributions; or</SPAN></P>
<P class="p758 ft5"><SPAN class="ft27">(c)</SPAN><SPAN class="ft114">substantially increase their costs of further participation in the Fund.</SPAN></P>

forslag.lydelse: Riksdagen antar regeringens förslag till lag om ändring i lagen (2023:907) om ändring i lagen (2023:440) om ändring i lagen (2022:1857) om ändring i lagen (2022:1042) om ändring i socialförsäkringsbalken (avsnitt 2 och 4.3).
Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen att öka Sveriges kvot i Internationella valutafonden med 2 215 000 000 särskilda dragningsrätter (avsnitt 5.2).
Riksdagen bemyndigar Riksbanken att till Internationella valutafonden betala det nödvändiga beloppet enligt 2 (avsnitt 5.2).

Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen att under 2024 för anslaget 1:1 Biståndsverksamhet inom utgiftsområde 7 Internationellt bistånd besluta om kapitaltillskott till Swedfund International AB på högst 300 000 000 kronor för investeringar i Ukraina (avsnitt 5.7).

Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen att ställa ut statliga garantier till Afrikanska utvecklingsbanken som inklusive tidigare utfärdade garantier uppgår till högst 3 054 240 000 Units of Account (avsnitt 5.7).

Riksdagen godkänner avtalet med Europeiska investeringsbanken om bidrag på sammanlagt högst 12 250 000 euro till den nyinrättade förvaltningsfonden för Afrika, Karibien och Stillahavsområdet ACP Trust Fund avseende tekniskt stöd, rådgivningstjänster, investeringsgarantier, räntekostnader och valutasäkring i lokala valutor som avser utvecklingsinstrument med hög finansiell risk i de minst utvecklade länderna (avsnitt 5.7).
Riksdagen godkänner målet för integrationspolitiken (avsnitt 5.13).

Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen att under 2024-2026 för anslaget 2:18 Kungl. Tekniska högskolan: Forskning och utbildning på forskarnivå inom utgiftsområde 16 Utbildning och universitetsforskning besluta om en årlig medlemsavgift till European Research Infrastructure for Imaging Technologies in Biological and Biomedical Sciences (Euro-Bioimaging-ERIC) på högst 2 000 000 kronor (avsnitt 5.16).
Riksdagen godkänner den föreslagna användningen av anslaget 3:1 Vetenskapsrådet: Forskning och forskningsinformation inom utgiftsområde 16 Utbildning och universitetsforskning (avsnitt 5.16).

Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen, eller den myndighet som regeringen bestämmer, att under 2024 för anslaget 3:1 Vetenskapsrådet: Forskning och forskningsinformation inom utgiftsområde 16 Utbildning och universitetsforskning för statens räkning förvärva aktier till ett belopp om högst 10 000 000 kronor i samband med att aktier tecknas i det bolag som övertar verksamheten i EISCAT Scientific Association (avsnitt 5.16).
Riksdagen godkänner den föreslagna användningen av anslaget 1:11 Trängselskatt i Stockholm inom utgiftsområde 22 Kommunikationer (avsnitt 5.22).
Riksdagen godkänner den föreslagna användningen av anslaget 1:12 Transportstyrelsen inom utgiftsområde 22 Kommunikationer (avsnitt 5.22).

Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen att för 2024 besluta om en kredit i Riksgäldskontoret för att tillgodose Tranportstyrelsens behov av rörelsekapital som inklusive tidigare utnyttjad kredit uppgår till högst 2 150 000 000 kronor (avsnitt 5.22).
Riksdagen godkänner den föreslagna användningen av anslaget 1:2 Insatser för skogsbruket inom utgiftsområde 23 Areella näringar, landsbygd och livsmedel (avsnitt 5.23).
Riksdagen godkänner den föreslagna användningen av anslaget 1:6 Bekämpning av smittsamma djursjukdomar inom utgiftsområde 23 Areella näringar, landsbygd och livsmedel (avsnitt 5.23).

Riksdagen godkänner den föreslagna användningen av anslaget 1:27 Åtgärder för beredskap inom livsmedels- och dricksvattenområdet inom utgiftsområde 23 Areella näringar, landsbygd och livsmedel (avsnitt 5.23).
Riksdagen godkänner den föreslagna användningen av anslaget 1:22 Stöd vid korttidsarbete inom utgiftsområde 24 Näringsliv (avsnitt 5.24).

Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen att för 2024 besluta att Aktiebolaget Svensk Exportkredit får ta upp lån i Riksgäldskontoret för exportfinansiering som inklusive tidigare upplåning uppgår till högst 150 000 000 000 kronor (avsnitt 5.24).
Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen att under 2024 ställa ut kreditgarantier för exportkrediter som inklusive tidigare utfärdade garantier uppgår till högst 500 000 000 000 kronor (avsnitt 5.24).
Riksdagen godkänner ändrade ramar för utgiftsområden och anvisar ändrade anslag enligt tabell 1.1.

Riksdagen bemyndigar regeringen att under 2024 ingå ekonomiska åtaganden som inklusive tidigare åtaganden medför behov av framtida anslag på högst de belopp och inom de tidsperioder som anges i tabell 1.2.
Riksdagen godkänner att Riksdagsförvaltningen får finansiera förvärvet av fastigheten Havssvalget 5 i dess helhet med anslag (avsnitt 5.1).
Riksdagen godkänner investeringsplanen för 2024-2026 för anslaget 2:3 Riksdagens fastighetsanslag som en riktlinje för Riksdagsförvaltningens fastighetsinvesteringar (avsnitt 5.1).
Riksdagen anvisar ändrat anslag som står till Riksdagsförvaltningens disposition enligt tabell 1.1.
